            "line": 7,
            "text": "// WHY `Value` IS DECLARED HERE. `Value` is `serde_json::Value`. specta"

          {
            "line": 8,
            "text": "// 2.0.0-rc.24 expands it INLINE at each use site, but its recursive arms cannot be"

            "line": 10,
            "text": "// `{ [key in string]: Value }`) while never emitting the declaration — leaving the"

          {

            "text": "// regeneration (typecheck-ratchet.test.ts's history note records restoring the"
          },

          {
            "line": 18,
            "text": "//"
          },
          {
            "line": 19,
            "text": "// EI-18899708711154370 · no-http-anywhere-2026-07-28 D-014."
          },
          {
            "line": 20,
            "text": "export type Value = \"Null\" | ({ Bool: boolean }) & { Array?: never; Number?: never; Object?: never; String?: never } | ({ Number: ({ f64: number }) & { i64?: never; u64?: never } | ({ i64: number }) & { f64?: never; u64?: never } | ({ u64: number }) & { f64?: never; i64?: never } }) & { Array?: never; Bool?: never; Object?: never; String?: never } | ({ String: string }) & { Array?: never; Bool?: never; Number?: never; Object?: never } | ({ Array: Value[] }) & { Bool?: never; Number?: never; Object?: never; String?: never } | ({ Object: { [key in string]: Value } }) & { Array?: never; Bool?: never; Number?: never; String?: never };"
          },
          {
            "line": 21,
            "text": "// This file has been generated by Tauri Specta. Do not edit this file manually."
          },
          {
            "line": 22,
            "text": ""
          },
          {
            "line": 23,
            "text": "import { invoke as __TAURI_INVOKE, Channel } from \"@tauri-apps/api/core\";"
          },
          {
            "line": 24,
            "text": "import * as __TAURI_EVENT from \"@tauri-apps/api/event\";"
          },
          {
            "line": 85,
            "text": "\t *  Spawn a new native pty and start a reader thread that emits"
          },
          {
            "line": 86,
            "text": "\t *  `pty-data` events as bytes arrive. Returns an id the renderer uses"
          },
          {
            "line": 87,
            "text": "\t *  for subsequent write/resize/kill calls."
          },
          {
            "line": 88,
            "text": "\t */"
          },
          {
            "line": 89,
            "text": "\tptySpawn: (opts: PtySpawnOpts) => typedError<PtySpawnResult, string>(__TAURI_INVOKE(\"pty_spawn\", { opts })),"
          },
          {
            "line": 90,
            "text": "\tptyWrite: (id: string, data: string) => typedError<null, string>(__TAURI_INVOKE(\"pty_write\", { id, data })),"
          },
          {
            "line": 91,
            "text": "\tptyResize: (id: string, cols: number, rows: number) => typedError<null, string>(__TAURI_INVOKE(\"pty_resize\", { id, cols, rows })),"
          },
          {
            "line": 92,
            "text": "\tptyKill: (id: string) => typedError<null, string>(__TAURI_INVOKE(\"pty_kill\", { id })),"
          },
          {
            "line": 93,
            "text": "\t/**"
          },
          {
            "line": 94,
            "text": "\t *  Return the persistent history buffer for a pty as base64. Used by"
          },
          {
            "line": 95,
            "text": "\t *  PiPanel on remount: the new xterm starts blank and replays history"
          },
          {
            "line": 96,
            "text": "\t *  to reach the same on-screen state. Empty string if the pty is"
          },
          {
            "line": 97,
            "text": "\t *  unknown or the history is empty."
          },
          {
            "line": 98,
            "text": "\t */"
          },
          {
            "line": 99,
            "text": "\tptyHistory: (id: string) => typedError<string, string>(__TAURI_INVOKE(\"pty_history\", { id })),"
          },
          {
            "line": 100,
            "text": "\t/**"
          },
          {
            "line": 101,
            "text": "\t *  Whether a pty id is still alive. Lets the renderer fall through to"
          },
          {
            "line": 102,
            "text": "\t *  a fresh spawn when the resume id is stale."
          },
          {
            "line": 103,
            "text": "\t */"
          },
          {
            "line": 104,
            "text": "\tptyIsAlive: (id: string) => __TAURI_INVOKE<boolean>(\"pty_is_alive\", { id }),"
          },
          {
            "line": 105,
            "text": "\twslStatus: () => __TAURI_INVOKE<WslStatus>(\"wsl_status\"),"
          },
          {
            "line": 106,
            "text": "\twslInstall: () => typedError<null, WslOpError>(__TAURI_INVOKE(\"wsl_install\")),"
          },
          {
            "line": 107,
            "text": "\t/**"
          },
          {
            "line": 108,
            "text": "\t *  Re-launch the desktop app with admin elevation via PowerShell's"
          },
          {
            "line": 109,
            "text": "\t *  `Start-Process -Verb RunAs`. The current process exits as soon as"
          },
          {
            "line": 110,
            "text": "\t *  the elevated child is spawned. The user sees the UAC prompt,"
          },
          {
            "line": 191,
            "text": "\t/**"
          },
          {
            "line": 192,
            "text": "\t *  Tauri command — invoked from the webview. The wire shape mirrors"
          },
          {
            "line": 193,
            "text": "\t *  what `apps/operator/lib/transport-adapters/ipc-stream.ts` sends."
          },
          {
            "line": 194,
            "text": "\t */"
          },
          {
            "line": 195,
            "text": "\tendpointInvoke: (toolName: string, input: \"Null\" | ({ Bool: boolean }) & { Array?: never; Number?: never; Object?: never; String?: never } | ({ Number: ({ f64: number }) & { i64?: never; u64?: never } | ({ i64: number }) & { f64?: never; u64?: never } | ({ u64: number }) & { f64?: never; i64?: never } }) & { Array?: never; Bool?: never; Object?: never; String?: never } | ({ String: string }) & { Array?: never; Bool?: never; Number?: never; Object?: never } | ({ Array: Value[] }) & { Bool?: never; Number?: never; Object?: never; String?: never } | ({ Object: { [key in string]: Value } }) & { Array?: never; Bool?: never; Number?: never; String?: never }, channel: Channel<EndpointEvent>) => typedError<number, string>(__TAURI_INVOKE(\"endpoint_invoke\", { toolName, input, channel })),"
          },
          {
            "line": 196,
            "text": "\t// Tauri command — cancel an in-flight call."
          },
          {
            "line": 197,
            "text": "\tendpointCancel: (callId: number) => typedError<null, string>(__TAURI_INVOKE(\"endpoint_cancel\", { callId })),"
          },
          {
            "line": 198,
            "text": "\t/**"
          },
          {
            "line": 199,
            "text": "\t *  Tauri command — IPC bridge health, for humans and agents."
          },
          {
            "line": 200,
            "text": "\t * "
          },
          {
            "line": 201,
            "text": "\t *  The observability hole this fills (WI-6512): when `/api` silently stayed on"
          },
          {
            "line": 202,
            "text": "\t *  the capped HTTP transport there was no way to ask the app *why*. The only"
          },
          {
            "line": 203,
            "text": "\t *  signal was a startup line that named the wrong cause, so the actual state —"
          },
          {
            "line": 206,
            "text": "\t *  from `ss`, `/proc` and the JSON files, per investigation."
          },
          {
            "line": 207,
            "text": "\t * "
          },
          {
            "line": 208,
            "text": "\t *  Cheap and side-effect-free (one small filesystem read); safe to poll."
          },
          {
            "line": 209,
            "text": "\t */"
          },
          {
            "line": 210,
            "text": "\tendpointIpcStatus: () => typedError<IpcStatus, string>(__TAURI_INVOKE(\"endpoint_ipc_status\")),"

          },
          {
            "line": 213,
            "text": "\t/**"

          },

            "line": 215,

          },
          {
            "line": 216,

          }

          "path": "papercusp-desktop/bin/lib/distribution-profile.sh",

          "sha256": "5a63f9d8faf69317e93ce1a53568fdf8f943caab86323a98d178c97cea82d05a",
          "source": "# shellcheck shell=bash\n# The build's DEFAULT distribution profile, derived from the tree being built.\n#\n# open-source-release-2026-09-29 D-005 / P-019: a build of the PUBLIC (ELv2) source cut\n# must run the `public` profile, which switches off every Claude.ai subscription relay\n# (account pooling, OAuth bundle sync, cross-device account honoring — see\n# packages/operator-core/lib/anthropic-auth-policy.ts). The public export writes\n# MANIFEST.json at the repo root with \"target\": \"public\", so the tree itself says which\n# build it is: nobody building from the public repo has to remember an env var, and the\n# private monorepo (no such MANIFEST) keeps its historical `dogfood` default.\n#\n# An explicit PAPERCUSP_DISTRIBUTION_PROFILE still wins; callers apply that themselves.\n\n# default_distribution_profile <desktop-root>\ndefault_distribution_profile() {\n  local manifest=\"$1/../MANIFEST.json\"\n  if [[ -f \"$manifest\" ]] && grep -Eq '\"target\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*\"public\"' \"$manifest\"; then\n    echo public\n  else\n    echo dogfood\n  fi\n}\n"
        },

            "text": "  async function loadFromDir(\n    dir: string,\n    source: string,\n  ): Promise<LoadFromDirResult<TPlugin, TManifest>> {\n    const path = resolve(dir);\n    const manifest = await ports.readManifest(path);\n    // A directory with neither manifest nor entry point isn't a\n    // misconfigured plugin — it's not a plugin dir at all. Skip silently\n    // instead of polluting the error log.\n    if (!manifest) {\n      const entry = await ports.locateEntry(path);\n      if (!entry) return { skipped: 'not-a-plugin', path };\n      return { error: ports.invalidManifestError ?? 'missing or invalid manifest', path };\n    }\n    if (typeof manifest === 'object' && '__error' in manifest) {\n      return { error: (manifest as ManifestError).__error, path };\n    }\n\n    const excluded = ports.admitManifest?.(manifest as TManifest, source) ?? null;\n    if (excluded) return { skipped: 'excluded', path, reason: excluded };\n\n    // Alternate-runtime manifests (e.g. wasm/daemon) can short-circuit the\n    // JS entry/import/validate path entirely.\n    if (ports.runtimeDispatch) {\n      const dispatched = await ports.runtimeDispatch(manifest as TManifest, path, source);\n      if (dispatched) return dispatched;\n      // null → fall through to the JS path.\n    }\n\n    const entry = await ports.locateEntry(path);\n    if (!entry) return { error: ports.noEntryError ?? 'no entry point found', path };\n    const imported = await importEntry(entry);\n    if (!imported) return { error: `import returned null/non-object from ${entry}`, path };\n    if (typeof imported === 'object' && 'error' in imported) {\n      return { error: `import threw at ${entry}: ${(imported as { error: string }).error}`, path };\n    }\n    const plugin = imported as TPlugin;\n    if (ports.validatePlugin) {\n      const validationError = await ports.validatePlugin(plugin, manifest as TManifest);\n      if (validationError) return { error: validationError, path };\n    }\n    return { plugin, manifest: manifest as TManifest, path, source };\n  }\n"

            "startLine": 573,
            "endLine": 609,
            "text": "async function runtimeDispatch(\n  manifest: ManifestShape,\n  path: string,\n  source: string,\n): Promise<CoreLoadedPlugin<Plugin, ManifestShape> | { error: string; path: string } | null> {\n  const runtime = manifest.runtime;\n  // kind='pack' purity, runtime half (tool-distribution-granularity D-004):\n  // wasm/daemon manifests short-circuit validate() below, so the runtime-less\n  // rule for packs must gate HERE, before the dispatch.\n  if ((manifest as { kind?: string }).kind === 'pack' && runtime && runtime.kind !== 'js') {\n    return {\n      error: `pack \"${(manifest as { name?: string }).name ?? '?'}\" declares runtime.kind \"${runtime.kind}\" — a pack is runtime-less (js-loaded tool handlers only); use kind \"plugin\"`,\n      path,\n    };\n  }\n  if (runtime?.kind === 'wasm') {\n    if (!runtime.wasmPath) {\n      return { error: 'manifest.runtime.kind = \"wasm\" but runtime.wasmPath missing', path };\n    }\n    const wasmAbs = resolve(path, runtime.wasmPath);\n    try {\n      // Stat-only — actual instantiation happens at enable time so a\n      // browse over installed plugins doesn't pay the wasmtime startup\n      // cost. The shim records intent; the operator's plugin-host-runtime\n      // calls loadWasmPlugin() at enable.\n      await fs.stat(wasmAbs);\n    } catch {\n      return { error: `wasm artifact not found at ${wasmAbs}`, path };\n    }\n    return { plugin: makeWasmPluginShim(manifest, wasmAbs), manifest, path, source };\n  }\n  if (runtime?.kind === 'daemon') {\n    if (!runtime.daemonCommand || runtime.daemonCommand.length === 0) {\n      return { error: 'manifest.runtime.kind = \"daemon\" but runtime.daemonCommand missing/empty', path };\n    }\n    return { plugin: makeDaemonPluginShim(manifest), manifest, path, source };\n  }"

            "text": "export async function loadPlugins(opts: LoaderOptions = {}): Promise<{\n  loaded: LoadedPlugin[];\n  errors: Array<{ error: string; path: string }>;\n}> {\n  // Build the Papercusp search roots (precedence: project > harness >\n  // global). The generic kernel walks + dedupes them by plugin name\n  // (first-seen wins); the `~/.papercusp` root resolution + scope-recursion\n  // policy is the Papercusp-specific part that stays here.\n  const roots: DiscoverRoot[] = [];\n  if (opts.projectDir) {\n    roots.push({ pluginsDir: join(opts.projectDir, 'plugins'), source: 'project' });\n  }\n  for (const slug of opts.harnessSlugs ??             "text": "function workerPath(): string {\n  const here =\n    typeof __filename !== 'undefined' ? __filename : fileURLToPath(import.meta.url);\n  return resolve(dirname(here), 'cpu-task-worker.script.mjs');\n}\n\nfunction workerExecArgv(): string[] {\n  // File-based workers cannot inherit flags that describe the parent's stdin\n  // entry or process-wide report handling. Keep this policy aligned with the\n  // event-loop sentinel worker host.\n  const parentOnlyValueFlags = ['--input-type', '--report-directory', '--report-filename'];\n  return process.execArgv.filter((arg, i, args) =>\n    !parentOnlyValueFlags.some(flag =>\n      arg === flag || arg.startsWith(`${flag}=`) || (i > 0 && args[i - 1] === flag),\n    ) && arg !== '--report-on-fatalerror' && arg !== '--no-report-on-fatalerror',\n  );"

            "startLine": 1,

            "text": "/**\n * Worker script for cpu-task-worker.ts — handles CPU-heavy synchronous work\n * off the operator main thread:\n *\n *   serialize  → JSON.stringify (with BigInt→Number replacer)\n *   broad_tree_scan → TypeScript AST census detection for evidence freshness\n *\n * Runs in a dedicated worker_threads thread so the main event loop is free\n * during the blocking compute. Do not re-add it (scripts/check-no-wire-compression.mjs).\n *\n * Protocol (main → worker):\n *   { kind: 'serialize', id: number, value: unknown }\n *\n * Protocol (worker → main):\n *   { kind: 'ready' }\n *   { kind: 'serialize_ok', id: number, json: string }\n *   { kind: 'serialize_err', id: number, error: string }\n *\n * Plain ESM .mjs (no TypeScript transform) — same convention as\n * local-embedder-worker.script.mjs.\n */\n"

        "excerpts": [
          {
            "startLine": 1,
            "endLine": 32,
            "text": "/**\n * event-loop-sentinel.worker.ts — the sentinel body, running on a\n * `worker_threads` Worker so it keeps ticking while the MAIN event loop is\n * blocked. Started by `event-loop-sentinel-host.ts`; the decision itself lives\n * in the pure `event-loop-sentinel.ts`.\n *\n * ## Three measured facts this file is built on\n *\n * All three were verified empirically (2026-08-04, EI-19465075959589134) rather\n * than assumed, because each one silently breaks the feature if wrong.\n *\n * 1. **A worker keeps running while the main thread spins.** Probe: main thread\n *    blocked 3000 ms; the worker observed the freeze and decided at 600 ms of\n *    staleness. Had it been blocked too it would have reported ~3000 ms after\n *    the fact. This is the premise of the whole design.\n *\n * 2. **`console.log` from a worker DOES NOT ESCAPE a blocked main thread.** It\n *    is proxied through the parent port, so it queues behind the block — in the\n *    probe it printed only *after* the main loop was released. Since we SIGKILL,\n *    the process would die before it ever flushed: a mysterious death with no\n *    log line. `fs.writeSync(2, …)` goes straight to fd 2 and DID print during\n *    the block. **Never use console/`process.stderr.write` in this file.**\n *\n * 3. **This file may be `.ts`.** The repo convention for worker bodies is plain\n *    `.mjs` (`cpu-task-worker.script.mjs`) precisely to avoid a TypeScript\n *    transform in a worker. Measured: a Worker spawned from the tsx-run host\n *    (`npx tsx bin/hono-host.ts`) resolves and imports repo `.ts` fine. Staying\n *    in `.ts` lets this file import the SAME decider the tests exercise, which\n *    matters more here than convention — a hand-copied `.mjs` state machine\n *    could drift from the tested one, and a drifted copy of *this* logic\n *    SIGKILLs production. Spawn failure is handled fail-soft by the host, so a\n *    runtime where this does not load simply disables the sentinel."
          },

            "startLine": 45,
            "endLine": 65,
            "text": "import { workerData, parentPort } from 'node:worker_threads';\nimport { Session } from 'node:inspector';\nimport { join } from 'node:path';\nimport {\n  writeSync,\n  readFileSync,\n  readlinkSync,\n  openSync,\n  readSync,\n  closeSync,\n  mkdirSync,\n  readdirSync,\n  renameSync,\n  rmSync,\n  writeFileSync,\n} from 'node:fs';\n// EXPLICIT `.ts` EXTENSION IS LOAD-BEARING (see the sentinel import below).\n// prettier-ignore\n// eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/ban-ts-comment\n// @ts-ignore — the plain-node Worker requires an explicit .ts specifier; apps/operator does not enable allowImportingTsExtensions.\nimport { STALL_PROFILE_DEFAULTS, hotStackFields, shouldCaptureStallProfile, summarizeHotStacks, syncSpawnProducer, type CpuProfileLike, type StallProfileConfig } from './event-loop-stall-profile.ts';"

            "text": "  ctx: PapercuspContext,\n): Promise<void> {\n  const key = regKey(lp.plugin.name, ctx.installSlug);\n  if (isDaemonProviderPlugin(lp)) {\n    ctx.log(`daemon plugin ${lp.plugin.name} is a provider: served by its sandboxed provider daemon, no action daemon started`);\n    return;\n  }\n  const cmd = lp.runtime?.daemonCommand;\n  if (!cmd || cmd.length === 0) {\n    throw new Error(`daemon runtime requested but runtime.daemonCommand empty on ${lp.plugin.name}`);\n  }\n  const daemon = await import('@papercusp/plugin-loader/daemon');\n  const handle = await daemon.startDaemonPlugin({\n    pluginName: lp.plugin.name,\n    cmd,\n    cwd: lp.path,\n    restart: lp.runtime?.daemonRestart,\n    onLog: (line: string) => ctx.log(`[daemon ${lp.plugin.name}] ${line}`),\n  });\n  state.wasmHandles.set(key, handle);\n  ctx.log(`daemon plugin started: ${lp.plugin.name} (cmd=${cmd[0]})`);\n}\n\n/**\n * Invoke a manifest-declared WASM action via the live WasmPlugin handle.\n * Returns the plugin's response bytes. Throws if no WASM plugin is\n * registered for (pluginName, installSlug) — caller should ensureInitialized\n * first via the standard action-invoke path.\n */\nexport async function callWasmAction(args: {\n  pluginName: string;\n  installSlug: string;\n  actionName: string;\n  payload: Uint8Array;\n  origin?: 'core' | 'ui';\n}): Promise<{ ok: true; payload: Uint8Array } | { ok: false; error: string }> {\n  const state = await getPluginHost();\n  const handle = state.wasmHandles.get(regKey(args.pluginName, args.installSlug));\n  if (!handle) {\n    return { ok: false, error: `no WASM plugin loaded for (${args.pluginName}, ${args.installSlug})` };\n  }"

            "text": "  // wedge prevents — measured: the worker's reply queued until the block ended.\n  // Sized for SENTINEL_SAB_IDX (heartbeat + last-known lag percentiles), not\n  // just the heartbeat — see that layout's doc.\n  const sab = new SharedArrayBuffer(SENTINEL_SAB_INT32_LEN * Int32Array.BYTES_PER_ELEMENT);\n  const view = new Int32Array(sab);\n\n  let worker: Worker;\n  try {\n    const data: SentinelWorkerData = {\n      sab,\n      thresholds: cfg.thresholds,\n      observeIntervalMs: cfg.observeIntervalMs,\n      mode: cfg.mode,\n      pid: process.pid,\n      stallProfile: cfg.stallProfile,\n    };\n    // --input-type describes the parent's inline/STDIN entry. This worker loads\n    // a file, so inheriting it fails asynchronously with ERR_INPUT_TYPE_NOT_ALLOWED.\n    // Report paths and fatal-error reporting are process-wide Node options:\n    // explicit Worker execArgv rejects them with ERR_WORKER_INVALID_EXEC_ARGV.\n    // Keep loaders and worker-supported diagnostics (signal/exception reports).\n    // Remove both spellings of value options, including their separate values.\n    const parentOnlyValueFlags = ['--input-type', '--report-directory', '--report-filename'];\n    const execArgv = process.execArgv.filter((arg, i, args) =>\n      !parentOnlyValueFlags.some(flag =>\n        arg === flag || arg.startsWith(`${flag}=`) || (i > 0 && args[i - 1] === flag),\n      ) && arg !== '--report-on-fatalerror' && arg !== '--no-report-on-fatalerror',\n    );\n    worker = new Worker(opts.workerPath ?? workerPath(), { workerData: data, execArgv });"

              "lines": [
                "  if (r.uid !== null && !Number.isInteger(r.uid)) return null;",
                "  if (typeof r.startedAt !== 'number') return null;",
                "  return { pid: r.pid as number, port: r.port as number, uid: r.uid as number | null, startedAt: r.startedAt };",
                "}",
                "",
                "export function readEmbedSidecarRecord(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = process.env): EmbedSidecarRecord | null {",
                "  try {",
                "    return parseEmbedSidecarRecord(readFileSync(embedSidecarRecordPath(env), 'utf8'));",
                "  } catch {",
                "    return null;",
                "  }",
                "}",
                "",
                "/** Atomic 0600 write (tmp + rename) into a 0700 dir. A failure is logged, not",
                " *  thrown: this Server still uses the child it holds; only sibling adoption is lost. */",
                "function writeEmbedSidecarRecord(rec: EmbedSidecarRecord, env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = process.env): void {",
                "  const file = embedSidecarRecordPath(env);",
                "  try {",
                "    mkdirSync(path.dirname(file), { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });",
                "    const tmp = `${file}.${process.pid}.tmp`;",
                "    writeFileSync(tmp, JSON.stringify(rec), { mode: 0o600 });",
                "    renameSync(tmp, file);",
                "  } catch (err) {",
                "    console.warn('[embed-sidecar] could not record the sidecar address:', err instanceof Error ? err.message : err);",
                "  }"
              ]
            },
            {
              "start": 300,
              "end": 315,
              "lines": [
                "}): EmbedSidecarAdoptVerdict {",
                "  const { record, uid } = input;",
                "  if (record.uid !== uid) return { adopt: false, reason: `recorded by uid ${record.uid}, this process is uid ${uid}` };",
                "  if (!input.pidAlive) return { adopt: false, reason: `recorded pid ${record.pid} is not running as this uid` };",
                "  if (input.listenerUids !== null && uid !== null) {",
                "    if (input.listenerUids.length === 0) return { adopt: false, reason: `nothing listens on port ${record.port}` };",
                "    if (!loopbackListenerOwnedBy(input.listenerUids, uid)) {",
                "      return { adopt: false, reason: `port ${record.port} is held by uid(s) ${input.listenerUids.join(',')}` };",
                "    }",
                "  }",
                "  if (input.healthPid !== undefined && input.healthPid !== record.pid) {",
                "    return { adopt: false, reason: `/healthz on port ${record.port} reports pid ${input.healthPid}, not ${record.pid}` };",
                "  }",
                "  return { adopt: true };",
                "}",
                ""
              ]
            },
            {
              "start": 377,
              "end": 393,
              "lines": [
                "/** Fetch and parse /healthz at `url`, or null if nothing healthy answers.",
                " *  Returns the PAYLOAD, not a boolean: liveness alone cannot decide whether a",
                " *  sidecar is usable, because a long-running one is frozen at its build time",
                " *  and 404s every route added since (EI-19314150478401738). Callers that need",
                " *  a route pair this with verifySidecarFitness(). */",
                "export async function probeSidecarHealth(url: string, timeoutMs = 1500): Promise<unknown | null> {",
                "  const ctl = new AbortController();",
                "  const timer = setTimeout(() => ctl.abort(), timeoutMs);",
                "  try {",
                "    const res = await fetch(`${url.replace(/\\/$/, '')}/healthz`, { signal: ctl.signal });",
                "    if (!res.ok) return null;",
                "    return (await res.json()) as unknown;",
                "  } catch {",
                "    return null;",
                "  } finally {",
                "    clearTimeout(timer);",
                "  }"
              ]
            },
            {
              "start": 527,
              "end": 575,
              "lines": [
                "",
                "  // Spawn target. esbuild bundles EVERY module into the single serve.mjs, so in",

                "/** Pure OpenAI network/retry adapter; host admission, alerts, and escalation are injected. */",
                "export function buildOpenAiEmbedderCore(",
                "  apiKey: string,",
                "  opts: OpenAiEmbedderOpts = {},",
                "  hooks: OpenAiEmbedderHooks = {},",
                "): EmbedFn {",
                "  const maxAttempts = opts.maxAttempts ?? EMBED_MAX_ATTEMPTS;",
                "  const sleep = opts.sleep ?? realSleep;",
                "  const totalBudgetMs = opts.maxTotalWaitMs ?? EMBED_TOTAL_BUDGET_MS;",
                "  const markFailure = hooks.markFailure ?? (() => {});",
                "  const admission = hooks.admission?.();",
                "  return async (text: string, signal?: AbortSignal): Promise<number[]> => {",
                "    signal?.throwIfAborted();",
                "    let lastErr: Error | null = null;",
                "    let waitedMs = 0;",
                "    const embedDeadlineAt = Date.now() + totalBudgetMs;",
                "    for (let attempt = 0; attempt < maxAttempts; attempt++) {",
                "      signal?.throwIfAborted();",
                "      const remainingBudgetMs = embedDeadlineAt - Date.now();",
                "      if (remainingBudgetMs <= 0) break;",
                "      let serverHintMs: number | null = null;",
                "      let slot: { release(): void } | null | undefined;",
                "      try {",
                "        slot = await admission?.acquire(text, 'memory');",
                "      } catch (error) {",
                "        if (hooks.isBudgetExhausted?.(error)) markFailure();",
                "        throw error;",
                "      }",
                "      try {",
                "        signal?.throwIfAborted();",
                "        const fetchBudgetMs = embedDeadlineAt - Date.now();",
                "        if (fetchBudgetMs <= 0) throw new Error('openai_embed_budget_spent');",
                "        const response = await fetch('https://api.openai.com/v1/embeddings', {",
                "          method: 'POST',",
                "          headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', Authorization: `Bearer ${apiKey}` },",
                "          body: JSON.stringify({",
                "            model: OPENAI_EMBEDDER_MODEL,",
                "            input: text,",
                "            dimensions: EMBEDDER_DIM_SPECS.openai.targetDims,",
                "          }),",
                "          signal: AbortSignal.any([",
                "            ...(signal ? [signal] : []),",
                "            AbortSignal.timeout(Math.max(1, Math.min(EMBED_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS, fetchBudgetMs))),",
                "          ]),",
                "        });",
                "        signal?.throwIfAborted();",
                "        admission?.recordResponse(headersToRecord(response.headers));",
                "        if (response.ok) {",
                "          void hooks.clearAlert?.();",
                "          const json = (await response.json()) as { data: Array<{ embedding: number[] }> };",
                "          signal?.throwIfAborted();",
                "          return json.data[0].embedding;",
                "        }",
                "        const body = await response.text().catch(() => '');",
                "        if (response.status === 429 && /insufficient_quota/.test(body)) {",
                "          markFailure(Date.now(), { hard: true });",
                "          void hooks.maybeEscalate?.();",
                "          throw new Error(`openai_embed_quota_exhausted: ${body}`);",
                "        }",
                "        const error = new Error(`openai_embed_failed_${response.status}: ${body}`);",
                "        if (response.status !== 429 && response.status < 500) throw error;",
                "        serverHintMs = retryDelayFromHeaders(response.headers);",
                "        if (response.status === 429) admission?.penalize({ retryAfterMs: serverHintMs ?? undefined });",
                "        lastErr = error;",
                "      } catch (error) {",
                "        signal?.throwIfAborted();",
                "        if (",
                "          error instanceof Error &&",
                "          (/^openai_embed_failed_4(?!29)/.test(error.message) || /^openai_embed_quota_exhausted/.test(error.message))",
                "        ) throw error;",
                "        lastErr = error instanceof Error ? error : new Error(String(error));",
                "      } finally {",
                "        slot?.release();",
                "      }",
                "      if (attempt >= maxAttempts - 1) break;",
                "      let waitMs = nextEmbedBackoffMs(attempt, serverHintMs, waitedMs, opts);",
                "      if (waitMs == null) break;",
                "      waitMs = Math.min(waitMs, embedDeadlineAt - Date.now());",
                "      if (waitMs <= 0) break;",
                "      waitedMs += waitMs;",
                "      await sleep(waitMs, signal);",
                "      signal?.throwIfAborted();",
                "    }",
                "    markFailure();",
                "    void hooks.maybeEscalate?.();",
                "    throw lastErr ?? new Error('openai_embed_failed: retries exhausted');",
                "  };",
                "}"

          "source": "/**\n * Locate the BUNDLED node runtime as an absolute path.\n *\n * ## Why an absolute path is required, not a bare `node`\n *\n * A packaged install is not guaranteed to have node on PATH *at all*. The app\n * ships its own runtime — on macOS at\n * `/Applications/Papercusp GUI.app/Contents/Resources/sidecar/bin/node` — and\n * `main.rs` exports that directory as `PAPERCUSP_SIDECAR_BIN` for every\n * packaged/dev-sidecar boot. Any code that hands a bare `node` to a\n * *grandchild* process (a spawn whose PATH we do not control — notably git's\n * `ext::` transport command) therefore works on the dev box and fails on a real\n * install. Resolve the binary here and pass the absolute path instead.\n *\n * ## Why `process.execPath` is gated behind a basename check (EI-2114)\n *\n * In a PACKAGED Tauri build `process.execPath` is the Tauri/sidecar binary, not\n * node — handing it to something that expects a node interpreter breaks exactly\n * the installs this resolver exists to serve. It is only a valid candidate when\n * it really is a node binary. The basename filters candidates; an interpreter\n * probe establishes identity, including when a Bun executable is named node.\n *\n * The returned binary is always a plain node (never a tsx/loader wrapper), so a\n * caller whose stdout is a binary protocol can rely on it booting quietly —\n * provided the caller also strips `NODE_OPTIONS` from the child env.\n */\nimport { execFile } from 'node:child_process';\nimport { createHash } from 'node:crypto';\nimport { access, readFile, realpath } from 'node:fs/promises';\nimport * as path from 'node:path';\nimport { promisify } from 'node:util';\n\nasync function pathExists(p: string): Promise<boolean> {\n  try {\n    await access(p);\n    return true;\n  } catch {\n    return false;\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * The BUNDLED node, resolved cwd-independently. `null` when this process can't\n * see it (an extracted dev-source operator whose env lacks\n * PAPERCUSP_SIDECAR_BIN and whose execPath is a tsx wrapper, not plain `node`).\n */\nexport async function resolveBundledNode(): Promise<string | null> {\n  const sidecarBin = process.env.PAPERCUSP_SIDECAR_BIN;\n  const execBase = path.basename(process.execPath).toLowerCase();\n  const execIsNode = execBase === 'node' || execBase === 'node.exe';\n  const bundledNames = process.platform === 'win32' ? ['node.exe', 'node'] : ['node', 'node.exe'];\n  const candidates = [\n    ...(sidecarBin ? bundledNames.map(name => path.join(sidecarBin, name)) : []),\n    execIsNode ? process.execPath : '',\n  ].filter(Boolean).map(candidate => path.resolve(candidate));\n  for (const c of candidates) {\n    if (!(await pathExists(c))) continue;\n    try {\n      if ((await measureRuntimePin(c)).name === 'node') return c;\n    } catch { /* Unusable or unidentified runtimes never become a Node boundary. */ }\n  }\n  return null;\n}\n\nexport type ApplicationRuntimeName = 'node' | 'bun';\n\nexport interface ApplicationRuntimePin {\n  name: ApplicationRuntimeName;\n  executable: string;\n  binarySha256: string;\n  version: string;\n  platform: string;\n  arch: string;\n}\n\nexport interface ApplicationRuntimeCandidate {\n  candidateSha256: string;\n  sourceSha: string;\n  roles: string[];\n  entrypoint: string;\n  entrypointSha256: string;\n  /** Package-attested bootstrap code; arbitrary runtime preload arguments remain forbidden. */\n  preload?: { path: string; sha256: string };\n  node: ApplicationRuntimePin;\n  bun?: ApplicationRuntimePin;\n}\n\n/** Supplied by the canonical acceptance reader, never inferred from a file's existence. */\nexport interface ApplicationRuntimeAcceptance {\n  verdict: 'accepted';\n  evidenceRef: string;\n  candidateSha256: string;\n  sourceSha: string;\n  role: string;\n  binarySha256: string;\n  nodeBinarySha256: string;\n  entrypointSha256: string;\n  validUntil: number;\n}\n\nexport interface ApplicationRuntimeLaunchRequest {\n  candidate: ApplicationRuntimeCandidate;\n  role: string;\n  runtime?: ApplicationRuntimeName;\n  purpose?: 'operational' | 'isolated-candidate' | 'rollback';\n  runtimeArgs?: string[];\n  args?: string[];\n  env?: NodeJS.ProcessEnv;\n  acceptanceRef?: string;\n  /** The caller must resolve this reference through the existing acceptance authority. */\n  verifyAcceptance?: (ref: string) => Promise<ApplicationRuntimeAcceptance | null>;\n}\n\n// Promisified lazily on first call, never at module scope (EI-10161): an eager\n// promisify(execFile) throws at import time under a narrow node:child_process test mock.\nlet cachedExecRuntime: typeof execFile.__promisify__ | undefined;\nconst execRuntime = ((...args: Parameters<typeof execFile.__promisify__>) =>\n  (cachedExecRuntime ??= promisify(execFile))(...args)) as typeof execFile.__promisify__;\nconst sha256 = (bytes: Uint8Array) => createHash('sha256').update(bytes).digest('hex');\nconst SHA256 = /^[a-f0-9]{64}$/;\nconst RUNTIME_IDENTITY = `process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify({\n  name:process.versions.bun?'bun':'node',version:process.versions.bun||process.versions.node,\n  executable:process.execPath,platform:process.platform,arch:process.arch\n}))`;\n\nfunction assertRuntimePin(pin: ApplicationRuntimePin, name: ApplicationRuntimeName): void {\n  if (!pin || pin.name !== name || !path.isAbsolute(pin.executable ?? '')\n    || !SHA256.test(pin.binarySha256 ?? '')\n    || [pin.version, pin.platform, pin.arch].some(value => typeof value !== 'string' || !value)) {\n    throw new Error(`A complete explicit ${name} runtime pin is required`);\n  }\n}\n\nasync function measureRuntimePin(candidate: string, expectedSha256?: string): Promise<ApplicationRuntimePin> {\n  const executable = await realpath(candidate);\n  const binarySha256 = sha256(await readFile(executable));\n  // A pinned executable must be checked before any identity subprocess can run.\n  if (expectedSha256 && binarySha256 !== expectedSha256) throw new Error('Runtime binary digest mismatch');\n  // Identity probes must not inherit credentials, preloads, or a loader from the host.\n  const env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = {};\n  for (const key of ['SystemRoot', 'WINDIR', 'TEMP', 'TMP', 'TMPDIR', 'LANG']) {\n    if (process.env[key] !== undefined) env[key] = process.env[key];\n  }\n  const { stdout } = await execRuntime(executable, ['-e', RUNTIME_IDENTITY], {\n    env, timeout: 5000, maxBuffer: 8192, windowsHide: true,\n  });\n  const measured = JSON.parse(stdout);\n  const pin = { ...measured, executable, binarySha256 } as ApplicationRuntimePin;\n  if (!['node', 'bun'].includes(measured.name)) throw new Error('Unknown runtime interpreter');\n  assertRuntimePin(pin, measured.name);\n  if (await realpath(measured.executable) !== executable\n    || sha256(await readFile(executable)) !== binarySha256) {\n    throw new Error('Runtime binary changed during measurement');\n  }\n  return pin;\n}\n\nasync function verifyRuntimePin(pin: ApplicationRuntimePin): Promise<ApplicationRuntimePin> {\n  const measured = await measureRuntimePin(pin.executable, pin.binarySha256);\n  if (measured.binarySha256 !== pin.binarySha256) throw new Error('Runtime binary digest mismatch');\n  if (measured.name !== pin.name || measured.version !== pin.version\n    || measured.platform !== pin.platform || measured.arch !== pin.arch) {\n    throw new Error('Runtime identity does not match its pin');\n  }\n  return measured;\n}\n\n/** Measure package-attested bytes before exposing them to the launch selector. */\nexport async function measurePinnedApplicationRuntime(\n  executable: string,\n  binarySha256: string,\n): Promise<ApplicationRuntimePin> {\n  if (!path.isAbsolute(executable) || !SHA256.test(binarySha256)) {\n    throw new Error('An absolute runtime path and package digest are required');\n  }\n  return measureRuntimePin(executable, binarySha256);\n}\n\n/**\n * Extend bundled-runtime resolution for application launches. Node tooling above\n * retains its existing resolver. This returns an argv vector, never a shell command.\n * The caller owns artifact immutability, isolated-candidate confinement, and spawning;\n * resolving a descriptor is not evidence that the host or a platform passed acceptance.\n */\nexport async function resolveApplicationRuntimeLaunch(request: ApplicationRuntimeLaunchRequest) {\n  if (!request?.candidate || !Array.isArray(request.candidate.roles)\n    || (request.runtimeArgs !== undefined && !Array.isArray(request.runtimeArgs))\n    || (request.args !== undefined && !Array.isArray(request.args))) {\n    throw new Error('Malformed application runtime selection');\n  }\n  const { role, verifyAcceptance, acceptanceRef } = request;\n  const runtime = request.runtime ?? 'node';\n  const purpose = request.purpose ?? 'operational';\n  // Snapshot caller data before invoking asynchronous filesystem/acceptance readers.\n  const candidate = { ...request.candidate, node: { ...request.candidate.node },\n    bun: request.candidate.bun ? { ...request.candidate.bun } : undefined,\n    preload: request.candidate.preload ? { ...request.candidate.preload } : undefined,\n    roles: [...(request.candidate.roles ?? [])] };\n  const runtimeArgs = [...(request.runtimeArgs ?? [])];\n  const args = [...(request.args ?? [])];\n  const env = { ...(request.env ?? process.env) };\n  if (!/^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$/.test(role)\n    || !['node', 'bun'].includes(runtime)\n    || !['operational', 'isolated-candidate', 'rollback'].includes(purpose)) {\n    throw new Error('Invalid application runtime selection');\n  }\n  if (!SHA256.test(candidate.candidateSha256) || !/^[a-f0-9]{40,64}$/.test(candidate.sourceSha)\n    || !path.isAbsolute(candidate.entrypoint) || !SHA256.test(candidate.entrypointSha256)) {\n    throw new Error('An explicit pinned application artifact is required');\n  }\n  if (candidate.preload && (!path.isAbsolute(candidate.preload.path)\n    || !SHA256.test(candidate.preload.sha256))) {\n    throw new Error('An explicit pinned application preload is required');\n  }\n  if (!candidate.roles.length || candidate.roles.some(value => !/^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$/.test(value))\n    || new Set(candidate.roles).size !== candidate.roles.length || !candidate.roles.includes(role)) {\n    throw new Error('Runtime role is absent from the candidate role census');\n  }\n  assertRuntimePin(candidate.node, 'node');\n  if (purpose === 'rollback' && runtime !== 'node') throw new Error('Rollback selects retained Node');\n  if (runtime === 'bun') assertRuntimePin(candidate.bun!, 'bun');\n  const allowedArgs = runtime === 'node' ? ['--enable-source-maps', '--expose-gc'] : ['--smol'];\n  if (runtimeArgs.some(arg => !allowedArgs.includes(arg))\n    || args.some(arg => typeof arg !== 'string' || arg.includes('\\0'))) {\n    throw new Error('Unsupported runtime or application arguments');\n  }\n  for (const key of Object.keys(env)) {\n    if (/^(NODE_OPTIONS|NODE_PATH|BUN_OPTIONS)$/i.test(key)) delete env[key];\n  }\n  let accepted: ApplicationRuntimeAcceptance | null = null;\n  const assertAcceptance = () => {\n    if (!accepted || accepted.verdict !== 'accepted' || accepted.evidenceRef !== acceptanceRef\n      || accepted.candidateSha256 !== candidate.candidateSha256 || accepted.sourceSha !== candidate.sourceSha\n      || accepted.role !== role || accepted.binarySha256 !== candidate.bun!.binarySha256\n      || accepted.nodeBinarySha256 !== candidate.node.binarySha256\n      || accepted.entrypointSha256 !== candidate.entrypointSha256\n      || !Number.isFinite(accepted.validUntil) || accepted.validUntil <= Date.now()) {\n      throw new Error('Matching current candidate acceptance is required for operational Bun');\n    }\n  };\n  if (runtime === 'bun' && purpose === 'operational') {\n    if (!acceptanceRef || !verifyAcceptance) throw new Error('Canonical Bun acceptance reader and reference required');\n    const receipt = await verifyAcceptance(acceptanceRef);\n    accepted = receipt ? { ...receipt } : null;\n    assertAcceptance();\n  }\n  const verifyEntrypoint = async () => {\n    if (sha256(await readFile(candidate.entrypoint)) !== candidate.entrypointSha256) {\n      throw new Error('Application entrypoint digest mismatch');\n    }\n    if (candidate.preload && sha256(await readFile(candidate.preload.path)) !== candidate.preload.sha256) {\n      throw new Error('Application preload digest mismatch');\n    }\n  };\n  await verifyEntrypoint();\n  // A Bun selection must keep the explicitly pinned Node rollback executable usable.\n  const node = await verifyRuntimePin(candidate.node);\n  const selected = runtime === 'node' ? node : await verifyRuntimePin(candidate.bun!);\n  await verifyEntrypoint();\n  if (accepted) assertAcceptance();\n  const preloadArgs = candidate.preload\n    ? [runtime === 'bun' ? '--preload' : '--require', candidate.preload.path] : [];\n  return { executable: selected.executable, args: [...runtimeArgs, ...preloadArgs, candidate.entrypoint, ...args], env,\n    runtime: selected, nodeRollback: node, candidateSha256: candidate.candidateSha256,\n    role, purpose, acceptanceRef: accepted?.evidenceRef ?? null };\n}\n",

          "source": "/**\n * Shared managed-child-process primitives (WI-3079, plan\n * clear-papercusp-backlog-2026-07-02).\n *\n * Extracted from the THIRD near-identical clone of the sidecar spawn +\n * respawn-with-backoff + graceful-stop shape:\n *   - sync/hyperbee/substrate-sidecar-spawn.ts   (scope-isolated, IPC handle transfer)\n *   - fleet/spawner-sidecar-spawn.ts             (simplest — but it DOES respawn)\n *   - inference-gateway/gateway-sidecar-spawn.ts (port-probe adoption, no scope isolation)\n *   - memory/embed-sidecar-spawn.ts              (also consumes these primitives)\n *\n * WHY these live here rather than being fully merged into one \"ManagedSidecar\"\n * orchestrator class: the three spawners genuinely differ in ways that are not\n * accidental duplication — substrate needs systemd-scope isolation + a raw-socket\n * IPC handle-transfer channel + a self-recursive scope-failure fallback; gateway\n * needs a TCP-listening ADOPTION probe (don't double-bind an externally-owned\n * port) + a continuous exit-driven respawn loop with re-probe-before-respawn;\n * spawner is the simplest orchestration of the set — but it DOES respawn\n * (MAX_RESPAWN_ATTEMPTS=5 over a 5-min sliding window with a give-up circuit\n * breaker, spawner-sidecar-spawn.ts:53-87). This line claimed \"no\n * respawn/circuit-breaker at all\" until 2026-08-04; it was false, and it was\n * read and believed, producing a wrong risk assessment of the bg-host cgroup\n * work (EI-19479764372783341). Forcing all of that into one\n * mega-config would trade three readable, independently-testable modules for one\n * harder-to-verify one, for a subsystem where a regression means a fleet-wide\n * agent-spawn / sync / inference outage. So this module extracts exactly the\n * pieces that ARE byte-identical (or identical-up-to-a-label) across all three —\n * the bundled-vs-dev spawn-plan resolution, the backoff + sliding-window\n * circuit-breaker bookkeeping, the SIGTERM→timeout→SIGKILL graceful-stop\n * sequence, and SIGTERM/SIGINT(+uncaughtException) shutdown-hook registration —\n * and leaves the top-level spawn/readiness/respawn orchestration local to each\n * file, where the genuine behavioral differences live. A further full-merge\n * remains a possible (riskier) follow-up if duplication resurfaces.\n */\n\nimport { readFileSync, statSync } from 'node:fs';\nimport { createRequire } from 'node:module';\nimport { dirname, join } from 'node:path';\n\n// ── bundled-vs-dev-tsx spawn-plan resolution ────────────────────────────────\n// esbuild bundles EVERY module into one serve.mjs; in a PACKAGED build\n// `import.meta.url` for the spawn module IS the bundle (no tsx, no .ts on\n// disk), so we re-exec that same artifact under the bundled node with a\n// divert env var the entrypoint checks for. In DEV (tsx, real source tree)\n// we run the sibling .ts entry under the explicit Node with the maintained tsx loader. Identical across all three\n// spawners modulo the divert env var name and the dev entry path.\n\nexport interface SidecarSpawnPlan {\n  cmd: string;\n  args: string[];\n  /** Extra env entries to layer over process.env for the child. */\n  env: Record<string, string>;\n  mode: 'bundled-reexec' | 'dev-tsx';\n}\n\nexport interface ResolveSidecarSpawnPlanOpts {\n  /** This spawn module's own resolved file — `fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)`\n   *  of the CALLER, not of this shared module. Bundled iff it does NOT end in\n   *  `.ts`/`.tsx` (esbuild emits `.mjs`/`.js`). */\n  selfPath: string;\n  /** Absolute path to the dev-mode `.ts` entry point (the sidecar script). */\n  devScriptPath: string;\n  /** Env var name the bundled re-exec sets to '1' so the entrypoint diverts\n   *  into sidecar-server mode instead of the normal operator boot path. */\n  bundledModeEnvVar: string;\n  /** Explicit retained Node executable; a Bun parent must resolve its Node boundary. */\n  execPath: string;\n  /** THIS process's own pid (`process.pid`) — declared to the child as its\n   *  parent identity. Required, not optional: a spawner that forgets to declare\n   *  itself silently reintroduces EI-20493378309289396 (see below), and a type\n   *  error at every call site is the only thing that reliably prevents that. */\n  spawnerPid: number;\n  /** Optional maintained sibling bundle. Older installs keep re-execing self. */\n  bundledScriptName?: string;\n}\n\n/** Pure: decide HOW to spawn a sidecar child (bundled re-exec-self vs dev\n *  explicit Node + tsx <entry>). Exported for unit tests. Identical decision across all\n *  three sidecar spawners, modulo the divert env var name + dev entry path. */\nexport function resolveSidecarSpawnPlan(opts: ResolveSidecarSpawnPlanOpts): SidecarSpawnPlan {\n  const isBundled = !opts.selfPath.endsWith('.ts') && !opts.selfPath.endsWith('.tsx');\n  if (isBundled) {\n    let entry = opts.selfPath;\n    if (opts.bundledScriptName) {\n      const candidate = join(dirname(opts.selfPath), opts.bundledScriptName);\n      try {\n        const info = statSync(candidate);\n        if (info.isFile() && info.size > 0) entry = candidate;\n      } catch {\n        // Older installations have no sibling; preserve the full-entry divert.\n      }\n    }\n    return {\n      cmd: opts.execPath, // the bundled node (e.g. ./bin/node), re-exec'ing selfPath\n      args: [entry],\n      env: { [opts.bundledModeEnvVar]: '1', ...parentIdentityEnv(opts.spawnerPid) },\n      mode: 'bundled-reexec',\n    };\n  }\n  const isTs = opts.devScriptPath.endsWith('.ts');\n  return {\n    cmd: opts.execPath,\n    args: isTs ? ['--import', createRequire(import.meta.url).resolve('tsx'), opts.devScriptPath] : [opts.devScriptPath],\n    env: { ...parentIdentityEnv(opts.spawnerPid) },\n    mode: 'dev-tsx',\n  };\n}\n\n/**\n * (EI-20493378309289396) Re-declare THIS process as the child's parent, so the\n * child's parent-death watch checks the process that actually spawned it.\n *\n * `PAPERCUSP_DESKTOP_PARENT_PID` is set by main.rs's `spawn_serve` to the DESKTOP\n * pid, and every sidecar spawn layers `plan.env` over `...process.env` — so\n * without this the value is INHERITED and names our GRANDparent. The child then\n * arms `startSidecarParentDeathWatch()` (serve.ts:1363-1368, before the mode\n * divert), and `isOrphanedFromParent(desktopPid, ourPid)` compares two pids that\n * can NEVER be equal for a grandchild. It fires on the pre-arm immediate check\n * and SIGTERMs itself within ~40ms of every boot, forever:\n *\n *   `desktop parent pid 79217 is gone (now reparented to 79225, detected before\n *    the watch armed) — self-terminating instead of running orphaned`\n *\n * Measured on the macOS rig 2026-08-16: 1,134 identical lines over 3h10m while\n * pid 79217 was demonstrably alive, `:8788` refused the whole time, and the\n * respawn budget re-armed every 60s to burn 5 more attempts. Independently filed\n * from a fresh Ubuntu 24.04 0.0.16 deb, so it is not platform-specific.\n *\n * This is the same CLASS as WI-37736 (a Windows pid compared against a WSL2 Linux\n * ppid) and takes the same shape of fix: stop a pid that means something else from\n * crossing a spawn boundary. Declaring OUR pid is the semantically correct\n * contract — the child's parent is us, and if WE die it SHOULD self-terminate —\n * and it keeps `declaredByLauncher` true, so the child retains the stronger\n * \"is that parent still alive?\" check rather than degrading to reparent-only.\n *\n * ⚠ Do NOT \"fix\" this by deleting the var instead: that silently downgrades the\n * child to `PROCESS_START_PPID` fallback semantics, which cannot detect a parent\n * that dies while the child is still booting (the EI-19486216732882752 race).\n */\nfunction parentIdentityEnv(spawnerPid: number): Record<string, string> {\n  return { PAPERCUSP_DESKTOP_PARENT_PID: String(spawnerPid) };\n}\n\n// ── per-host sidecar enable-check (WI-3793) ─────────────────────────────────\n// Every node-child sidecar (substrate/spawner/gateway/embed) is switched on by\n// a PER-HOST env opt-in the operator sets on the bg-host systemd unit (e.g.\n// PAPERCUSP_SPAWNER_SIDECAR=1) — distinct from the bundled-reexec DIVERT var\n// above (PAPERCUSP_SPAWNER_SIDECAR_MODE) that only the parent's OWN spawn code\n// sets on the re-exec'd child, telling its entrypoint \"boot as the sidecar\n// server, not the normal host\". Before this, each caller of the enable-check\n// (run-git-sync.ts's gitSyncSidecarEnabled, host-bootstrap.ts's pre-warm\n// gate, orchestrator-runner.ts's spawnInvokeOnceWithFallback gate) hand-rolled\n// its own `process.env.PAPERCUSP_SPAWNER_SIDECAR === '1'` inline — 3\n// near-duplicated checks, and only git-sync's ALSO guarded against the enable\n// var being inherited into the sidecar's own re-exec'd child (which spreads\n// `...process.env` for the child, per spawnSpawnerSidecar above) and\n// mis-firing there. Today that's masked in practice (every sidecar spawn\n// explicitly clears PAPERCUSP_BACKGROUND_WORKERS for the child, and none of\n// the 2 unguarded call sites currently run inside a sidecar child) — but it's\n// a latent footgun, not a designed invariant. One shared, defensively-guarded\n// implementation now backs every call site instead of 3 divergent ones; see\n// isSidecarEnabledFromEnv below.\n\n/**\n * Why a sidecar cannot serve this caller. `unreachable` = nothing answered\n * /healthz. `stale-build` = it answered but advertises NO capability list at\n * all, i.e. it was built before capability advertisement existed, and the\n * routes the caller needs postdate it. `missing-capabilities` = it advertises\n * a list and the caller's requirements are not in it.\n */\nexport type SidecarUnfitReason = 'unreachable' | 'stale-build' | 'missing-capabilities';\n\nexport type SidecarFitness =\n  | { fit: true }\n  | { fit: false; reason: SidecarUnfitReason; missing: string[] };\n\n/**\n * Pure: can the sidecar described by `health` serve everything in `required`?\n *\n * A sidecar is a long-running process started from a BUILT BUNDLE, so it is\n * frozen at its build time while its callers keep advancing. Liveness is\n * therefore NOT fitness: a 16-day-old sidecar answers /healthz 200 and still\n * 404s every route added since it was built, forever, for every process that\n * adopts it — and each caller's fail-safe converts that 404 into a silent\n * degradation (EI-19314150478401738).\n *\n * `legacyCapabilities` is what a health payload with NO `capabilities` key may\n * be credited with — the routes that have existed for the whole life of the\n * artifact. Crediting a pre-advertisement build with exactly those (and never\n * more) is what lets an old sidecar keep serving its original routes without\n * being trusted for newer ones.\n */\nexport function verifySidecarFitness(\n  health: unknown | null,\n  required: readonly string[],\n  legacyCapabilities: readonly string[] = [],\n): SidecarFitness {\n  if (health === null || health === undefined || typeof health !== 'object') {\n    return { fit: false, reason: 'unreachable', missing: [...required] };\n  }\n  const raw = (health as { capabilities?: unknown }).capabilities;\n  const declared = Array.isArray(raw) ? raw.filter((c): c is string => typeof c === 'string') : null;\n  // No advertisement ⇒ a pre-capability build. Credit it with the historical\n  // floor only; anything beyond that is a route it provably cannot have.\n  const effective = declared ?? legacyCapabilities;\n  const missing = required.filter((c) => !effective.includes(c));\n  if (missing.length === 0) return { fit: true };\n  return {\n    fit: false,\n    reason: declared === null ? 'stale-build' : 'missing-capabilities',\n    missing,\n  };\n}\n\nexport interface SidecarEnabledOpts {\n  /** Per-host opt-in enable var, e.g. 'PAPERCUSP_SPAWNER_SIDECAR'. */\n  enableVar: string;\n  /** Bundled-reexec divert var (see SidecarSpawnPlan), e.g.\n   *  'PAPERCUSP_SPAWNER_SIDECAR_MODE'. Reading '1' here means THIS process IS\n   *  the re-exec'd sidecar child — always resolves disabled, regardless of\n   *  what the (possibly-inherited) enable var reads, so the enable-check can\n   *  never fire recursively inside the sidecar it gates. */\n  modeVar: string;\n  /** Optional explicit per-caller override var (e.g.\n   *  'PAPERCUSP_GIT_SYNC_SPAWN_SIDECAR') checked BEFORE `enableVar` when\n   *  present (non-null) — '1'/'true' forces ON, anything else forces OFF,\n   *  either way short-circuiting `enableVar`. Absent/unset falls through to\n   *  the plain enable-var check. */\n  explicitVar?: string;\n}\n\n/** Pure: is a per-host-gated sidecar enabled for the CURRENT process? Exported\n *  for unit tests; `env` defaults to `process.env` for callers. */\nexport function isSidecarEnabledFromEnv(\n  opts: SidecarEnabledOpts,\n  env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = process.env,\n): boolean {\n  if (env[opts.modeVar] === '1') return false;\n  if (opts.explicitVar) {\n    const explicit = env[opts.explicitVar];\n    if (explicit != null) return explicit === '1' || explicit === 'true';\n  }\n  return env[opts.enableVar] === '1';\n}\n\n// ── respawn backoff + sliding-window circuit breaker ────────────────────────\n\n/** Backoff before respawn attempt N (1-based) within the window: 1s·2^(N−1),\n *  capped at `capMs` (default 30s). Identical formula across all FOUR\n *  respawn-capable spawners: embed-sidecar-spawn, substrate-sidecar-spawn,\n *  gateway-sidecar-spawn AND fleet/spawner-sidecar-spawn.\n *\n *  ⚠ This said \"all three … (spawner-sidecar-spawn.ts has no respawn at all)\"\n *  until 2026-08-04, which was false and self-contradicting: that file calls\n *  THIS function at :78 and has MAX_RESPAWN_ATTEMPTS=5 over a 5-min sliding\n *  window with a give-up circuit breaker (:53-87). Corrected by counting the\n *  callers rather than trusting the sentence — it had already been used to\n *  justify a wrong risk assessment of the bg-host cgroup fix\n *  (EI-19479764372783341). Re-count before editing this line. */\nexport function respawnBackoffMs(attemptInWindow: number, capMs = 30_000): number {\n  return Math.min(1000 * 2 ** Math.max(0, attemptInWindow - 1), capMs);\n}\n\n/** Drop timestamps older than `windowMs` from a sliding respawn-attempt window. */\nexport function pruneRespawnWindow(attempts: number[], now: number, windowMs: number): number[] {\n  return attempts.filter((t) => now - t < windowMs);\n}\n\n/** Has the circuit breaker tripped (>= maxAttempts within the current window)? */\nexport function respawnBudgetExhausted(attempts: number[], maxAttempts: number): boolean {\n  return attempts.length >= maxAttempts;\n}\n\n// ── graceful SIGTERM→timeout→SIGKILL stop sequence ──────────────────────────\n\nexport interface KillableChild {\n  once(event: 'exit', listener: () => void): void;\n}\n\n/** Signal `child`, wait up to `timeoutMs` for its 'exit', force-kill if it\n *  doesn't. Resolves either way — never rejects. Callers own their own state\n *  resets (a `ready` flag, nulling a module-global process handle, a\n *  process-TREE group-kill instead of a single-pid kill, …) since those are\n *  exactly where the three spawners differ; this only sequences the signal +\n *  wait, which was previously copy-pasted three times almost verbatim. */\nexport function gracefulStopChild(\n  child: KillableChild,\n  opts: { timeoutMs: number; kill: (sig: NodeJS.Signals) => void },\n): Promise<void> {\n  return new Promise<void>((resolve) => {\n    const timeout = setTimeout(() => {\n      try {\n        opts.kill('SIGKILL');\n      } catch {\n        /* already gone */\n      }\n      resolve();\n    }, opts.timeoutMs);\n    (timeout as unknown as { unref?: () => void }).unref?.();\n    child.once('exit', () => {\n      clearTimeout(timeout);\n      resolve();\n    });\n    try {\n      opts.kill('SIGTERM');\n    } catch {\n      clearTimeout(timeout);\n      resolve();\n    }\n  });\n}\n\n// ── shutdown-hook registration ───────────────────────────────────────────────\n\nexport interface SidecarShutdownHooksOpts {\n  /** Log-line prefix, e.g. 'substrate-sidecar-spawn'. Also the idempotency key. */\n  label: string;\n  /** Called on SIGTERM/SIGINT (async mode also covers uncaughtException). */\n  stop: () => void | Promise<void>;\n  /**\n   * 'async' (default): SIGTERM/SIGINT/uncaughtException each log then `await\n   * stop()` — the substrate + spawner shape. Fatal exceptions preserve the\n   * original error and a nonzero exit status without forcing the host to exit\n   * before its teardown completes.\n   * 'async-with-exit': the async signal/exception behavior above, plus an\n   * exit listener that begins `stop()` synchronously before Node tears down\n   * the event loop. This is for children that must not survive a short-lived\n   * host's normal `process.exit()` path.\n   * 'sync-with-exit': also listens on Node's 'exit' event, whose handlers\n   * MUST run synchronously (an async continuation there is silently dropped\n   * once the process has already begun exiting) — no logging, fires\n   * `void stop()` fire-and-forget. The gateway supervisor's shape (it must\n   * catch the \"operator exited without a signal\" case too).\n   */\n  mode?: 'async' | 'async-with-exit' | 'sync-with-exit';\n  /**\n   * Async modes ONLY: gate the `uncaughtException` reaction on whether this\n   * particular exception is genuinely fatal to the HOST process. Node fires\n   * `uncaughtException` listeners process-wide for EVERY uncaught exception,\n   * not just ones related to this sidecar — so without a filter, an error the\n   * host's OWN guard already classifies as benign and swallows (e.g. hono-host's\n   * `isBenignHostError` — a client-disconnect `write EPIPE`, a torn-down PG\n   * connection, …) ALSO reaches this listener and tears down a perfectly\n   * healthy sidecar, which then gets warm-respawned by the next caller (the\n   * P-006 \"spawner-sidecar respawn churn\" — a `[swarm] DHT bootstrap` line and\n   * a fresh child every few minutes on ordinary client-disconnect traffic,\n   * long after the EI-8810 EADDRINUSE divert was fixed). Default: always fatal\n   * (`() => true`) — preserves prior behavior for a caller that doesn't pass one.\n   */\n  isFatalException?: (err: unknown) => boolean;\n  /**\n   * EI-24863236643374267: asked at SIGTERM/SIGINT time. When it returns true the\n   * signal listener does NOT stop the sidecar; the caller has arranged a later stop\n   * (the spawner registers one with shutdown-state's onBeforeHostExit, which the\n   * host's graceful drain runs right before it exits). Without this the sidecar is\n   * stopped BEFORE the drain starts, because this listener is registered at spawn\n   * time, ahead of the drain's own — and every git call made during the drain then\n   * forks on the host's main thread. Default: never defer.\n   */\n  deferStopToHostExit?: () => boolean;\n}\n\nconst hooksRegisteredFor = new Set<string>();\n\n/** Register shutdown hooks exactly once per `label` (idempotent — calling\n *  this twice for the same label is a no-op the second time, closing a latent\n *  double-registration gap the original substrate/spawner versions had). */\nexport function registerSidecarShutdownHooks(opts: SidecarShutdownHooksOpts): void {\n  if (hooksRegisteredFor.has(opts.label)) return;\n  hooksRegisteredFor.add(opts.label);\n\n  if (opts.mode === 'sync-with-exit') {\n    const sync = () => {\n      void opts.stop();\n    };\n    process.on('exit', sync);\n    process.on('SIGTERM', sync);\n    process.on('SIGINT', sync);\n    return;\n  }\n\n  if (opts.mode === 'async-with-exit') {\n    // `stop()` begins synchronously (it signals the child before its first\n    // await), which is the only useful work an async shutdown can do once the\n    // process has entered Node's `exit` event. The normal signal handlers below\n    // still await the full graceful-stop sequence.\n    process.on('exit', () => {\n      void opts.stop();\n    });\n  }\n\n  const onSignal = async (sig: 'SIGTERM' | 'SIGINT'): Promise<void> => {\n    if (opts.deferStopToHostExit?.()) {\n      console.log(`[${opts.label}] ${sig} received, keeping sidecar up until the host drain exits`);\n      return;\n    }\n    console.log(`[${opts.label}] ${sig} received, shutting down sidecar`);\n    await opts.stop();\n  };\n  process.on('SIGTERM', () => onSignal('SIGTERM'));\n  process.on('SIGINT', () => onSignal('SIGINT'));\n  const isFatal = opts.isFatalException ?? (() => true);\n  process.on('uncaughtException', async (err) => {\n    if (!isFatal(err)) {\n      // The host's own guard already classified + swallowed this one (kept the\n      // host alive) — an exception the host survives is not a reason to tear\n      // down an otherwise-healthy sidecar. Silent: hono-host's guard already\n      // logs the benign classification for this same error.\n      return;\n    }\n    // Installing a listener replaces Node's default fatal diagnostic/exit.\n    // Restore both without process.exit(), which would truncate owned cleanup.\n    if (process.exitCode === undefined || Number(process.exitCode) === 0) {\n      process.exitCode = 1;\n    }\n    console.error(`[${opts.label}] uncaught exception, shutting down sidecar:`, err);\n    try {\n      await opts.stop();\n    } catch (stopError) {\n      // An async event listener's rejection is otherwise unobserved and may\n      // re-enter uncaughtException under Node's unhandled-rejection policy.\n      console.error(`[${opts.label}] sidecar shutdown after uncaught exception failed:`, stopError);\n    }\n  });\n}\n\n/** Test seam — forget which labels have registered hooks. */\nexport function _resetSidecarShutdownHookRegistryForTests(): void {\n  hooksRegisteredFor.clear();\n}\n\n/** Test seam — which labels have registered shutdown hooks in this process.\n *  WI-7249: lets a guard assert that registration happened as a side effect of\n *  SPAWNING, without spawning a real child or counting raw process listeners\n *  (which every other module in the test process also adds to). */\nexport function _registeredSidecarShutdownLabelsForTests(): string[] {\n  return [...hooksRegisteredFor].sort();\n}\n\n// ── who owns a loopback port (P-530, WI-10005481 class) ─────────────────────\n// A sidecar answering /healthz on 127.0.0.1:<port> says nothing about WHOSE it\n// is. On a host shared by several tenants (one Linux user each), adopting a\n// sibling by liveness alone hands this tenant's text to another tenant's\n// process. The kernel's socket tables record the owning uid of every LISTEN\n// socket, so the question has a direct answer that no process can forge.\n\n/** `/proc/net/tcp{,6}` state code for LISTEN. */\nconst TCP_STATE_LISTEN = '0A';\n\n/** local_address hex forms a connection to 127.0.0.1 can land on: the\n *  loopback address itself (either byte order) and the IPv4 wildcard; for\n *  tcp6, the dual-stack wildcard `::` and `::ffff:127.0.0.1`. */\nconst LOOPBACK_REACHABLE_ADDRS = new Set([\n  '0100007F',\n  '7F000001',\n  '00000000',\n  '00000000000000000000000000000000',\n  '0000000000000000FFFF00000100007F',\n]);\n\n/**\n * Pure parser: the uids of every LISTEN socket in one `/proc/net/tcp`-format\n * table whose local address a connection to 127.0.0.1:`port` can reach.\n */\nexport function parseLoopbackListenerUids(tableText: string, port: number): number[] {\n  const uids: number[] = [];\n  for (const line of tableText.split('\\n').slice(1)) {\n    const f = line.trim().split(/\\s+/);\n    // sl local_address rem_address st tx:rx tr:when retrnsmt uid timeout inode\n    if (f.length < 8 || f[3] !== TCP_STATE_LISTEN) continue;\n    const sep = f[1].lastIndexOf(':');\n    if (sep < 0) continue;\n    if (Number.parseInt(f[1].slice(sep + 1), 16) !== port) continue;\n    if (!LOOPBACK_REACHABLE_ADDRS.has(f[1].slice(0, sep).toUpperCase())) continue;\n    const uid = Number(f[7]);\n    if (Number.isInteger(uid)) uids.push(uid);\n  }\n  return uids;\n}\n\n/**\n * The uids owning a LISTEN socket reachable at 127.0.0.1:`port`. `[]` = nothing\n * listens there. `null` = this host cannot answer (no readable\n * `/proc/net/tcp`, i.e. not Linux), and the caller must not treat that as\n * \"owned by me\".\n */\nexport function loopbackListenerUids(\n  port: number,\n  readTable: (path: string) => string | null = readProcTable,\n): number[] | null {\n  let readable = false;\n  const uids: number[] = [];\n  for (const table of ['/proc/net/tcp', '/proc/net/tcp6']) {\n    const text = readTable(table);\n    if (text === null) continue;\n    readable = true;\n    uids.push(...parseLoopbackListenerUids(text, port));\n  }\n  return readable ? uids : null;\n}\n\nfunction readProcTable(path: string): string | null {\n  try {\n    return readFileSync(path, 'utf8');\n  } catch (err) {\n    // Only a filesystem error (ENOENT on a non-Linux host, EACCES) means \"no\n    // table\". Anything else is a bug and must stay loud: a swallowed\n    // ReferenceError once made every ownership check here read \"unknown\".\n    if (err && typeof err === 'object' && typeof (err as { code?: unknown }).code === 'string') return null;\n    throw err;\n  }\n}\n\n/** May this process adopt whatever listens on 127.0.0.1:`port`? Only when every\n *  listener there belongs to `uid`. Unknown ownership (null) is a refusal on\n *  Linux-shaped hosts; a host with no socket table at all (`null` from\n *  {@link loopbackListenerUids}) is decided by the caller. */\nexport function loopbackListenerOwnedBy(uids: number[] | null, uid: number): boolean | null {\n  if (uids === null) return null;\n  return uids.length > 0 && uids.every((u) => u === uid);\n}\n",

            "text": "{\n  \"name\": \"@papercusp/memory\",\n  \"version\": \"0.1.0\",\n  \"private\": true,\n  \"type\": \"module\",\n  \"description\": \"Persistent-memory store behind a swappable MemoryBackend seam: neutral remember/search/list/forget/update verbs over {id,text,kind,scope,score,metadata}, a backend registry + selector (configureMemory({backend})), and three shipped impls — mem0 (mem0ai/oss + canonical pgvector store, per-embedder vec tables, local BGE embedder, re-embed pass), noop (clean 'no store'), and claude-file (Claude Code topic-file bridge). Host-agnostic — admin URL, LLM credentials, embedder, and backend choice are injected via configureMemory(). Zero @papercusp/@restart runtime deps.\",\n  \"main\": \"./src/index.ts\",\n  \"types\": \"./src/index.ts\",\n  \"exports\": {\n    \".\": {\n      \"types\": \"./src/index.ts\",\n      \"import\": \"./src/index.ts\",\n      \"default\": \"./src/index.ts\"\n    },\n    \"./bench\": {\n      \"types\": \"./src/bench/index.ts\",\n      \"import\": \"./src/bench/index.ts\",\n      \"default\": \"./src/bench/index.ts\"\n    }\n  },\n  \"scripts\": {\n    \"test\": \"vitest run\"\n  },\n  \"dependencies\": {\n    \"@papercusp/module-singleton\": \"*\",\n    \"pg\": \"^8.20.0\",\n    \"tokenizers\": \"0.23.2\"\n  },\n  \"optionalDependencies\": {\n    \"@huggingface/transformers\": \"4.2.0\"\n  },\n  \"devDependencies\": {\n    \"@types/pg\": \"^8.15.5\",\n    \"vitest\": \"^4.1.4\"\n  }\n}\n"

            "text": "/**\n * @papercusp/memory — the mem0-backed persistent-memory store core.\n *\n * Host-agnostic: the embedded-pg admin URL, LLM credentials, the resolved\n * embedder (a pre-built embed fn + mode + dims), the explicit-mode\n * embedder builder, and the optional adaptive-instruction feed are all\n * injected via `configureMemory()`. mem0 owns its own `pg.Client`, so\n * no shared transaction handle is injected.\n *\n * The operator's curation pipeline (learning loop, pre-turn injection,\n * harness anchoring, dedup judge, insights index) stays in the operator\n * and is built ON TOP of this store via the `memory:*` tool wrappers.\n *\n * Extracted per papercusp-systems-abstraction-2026-05-29 (P-021).\n */\n\nexport {\n  configureMemory,\n  memoryHost,\n  isMemoryConfigured,\n  type MemoryHost,\n  type MemoryCredentials,\n  type ResolvedEmbedder,\n  type EmbedFn,\n} from './config';\n\nexport {\n  getMemoryClient,\n  getResolvedMode,\n  getResolvedProfile,\n  invalidateMemoryClient,\n  disposeMemoryClient,\n  embedForCurrentClient,\n  vectorSearchCanonical,\n} from './mem0-client';\n\n// Injectable fact-extraction LLM seam (mem0-extraction-via-claude-session\n// D-003): hosts implement `ExtractionLlm` (mem0ai's LLM shape) and hand it\n// back from `MemoryHost.getExtractionLlm` to become cascade rung #1.\n// `ExtractionAuthError` is the typed throw that triggers a STICKY demotion\n// to the key rungs (D-004); `FallbackExtractionLlm` is the cascade wrapper\n// (exported for hosts that compose their own cascades + for tests).\nexport {\n  ExtractionAuthError,\n  FallbackExtractionLlm,\n  type ExtractionLlm,\n  type ExtractionLlmMessage,\n  type ExtractionLlmResponse,\n} from './extraction-llm';\n\n// The neutral, swappable store seam (generalize-memory-backend-swappable\n// D-001/D-002/D-004).             "text": "{\n  \"name\": \"@papercusp/rerank\",\n  \"version\": \"0.1.0\",\n  \"description\": \"Engine-agnostic cross-encoder reranking: a local ONNX cross-encoder (no key, no network) or the hosted ZeroEntropy zerank API. Shared across Papercusp and Restart.\",\n  \"license\": \"UNLICENSED\",\n  \"$comment_type\": \"MUST stay \\\"module\\\". This package is named-imported by ESM consumers (@papercusp/search-core, operator-core) running under tsx. As a TYPELESS package tsx transpiles it to CJS, and Node then links named imports via cjs-module-lexer — which cannot see `export … from` re-export chains, so the whole namespace links EMPTY and EVERY named import throws at runtime. Unit tests and tsc do NOT catch it (vitest/vite bundle instead of linking). Native ESM makes re-exports linkable.\",\n  \"type\": \"module\",\n  \"main\": \"src/index.ts\",\n  \"types\": \"src/index.ts\",\n  \"exports\": {\n    \".\": {\n      \"types\": \"./src/index.ts\",\n      \"import\": \"./src/index.ts\",\n      \"default\": \"./src/index.ts\"\n    }\n  },\n  \"sideEffects\": false,\n  \"scripts\": {\n    \"test\": \"vitest run --passWithNoTests\",\n    \"typecheck\": \"tsc --noEmit\"\n  },\n  \"dependencies\": {\n    \"@papercusp/module-singleton\": \"*\",\n    \"zeroentropy\": \"^0.1.0-alpha.10\"\n  },\n  \"peerDependencies\": {\n    \"@huggingface/transformers\": \">=4\"\n  },\n  \"peerDependenciesMeta\": {\n    \"@huggingface/transformers\": {\n      \"optional\": true\n    }\n  },\n  \"publishConfig\": {\n    \"access\": \"restricted\"\n  }\n}\n"
