            "gitBlob": "3215e591887d472275dbf3ead3ae96e121590384",
            "sha256": "8ce43e8d8fdf4c30d2bf7ed964e99616965ee6dbf57f0a05f950f67c2ec16660",
            "bytes": 17470,
            "text": "/**\n * @papercusp/rerank — engine-agnostic cross-encoder reranking.\n *\n * Stage B of the retrieve→rerank pipeline: given a query and candidate docs\n * (from ANY retriever — Typesense, Postgres, pgvector, …), reorder them by a\n * cross-encoder's relevance score. Has NO project-specific deps, so it can be\n * lifted into any consumer unchanged — the only per-project differences are the\n * config (engine, model, topN, threshold).\n *\n * Two engines, one contract:\n *   - `local`        — an ONNX cross-encoder in-process (no key, no network, no\n *                      per-call cost). See `local-engine.ts`.\n *   - `zeroentropy`  — the hosted zerank API (calibrated scores, instruction\n *                      following, someone else's GPU).\n *\n * Fail-safe by design: if the engine is unavailable or errors, it returns the\n * candidates in their ORIGINAL order — a rerank outage degrades to \"retrieval\n * order\", it never breaks search. Every engine funnels through the same\n * `EngineScores` seam below precisely so that guarantee is enforced in ONE\n * place and cannot be re-litigated per engine.\n */\nimport ZeroEntropy from 'zeroentropy';\n\nimport { type LocalRerankOptions, localEngineScores, scoreCrossEncoder } from './local-engine';\nimport { isDeadlineFailure } from './scorer-gate';\nimport type { RerankScoreFn } from './sidecar-reranker';\n\nexport {\n  RERANK_MAX_CONCURRENT_ENV,\n  RerankDeadlineError,\n  getScorerGateState,\n  isDeadlineFailure,\n  runInScorerGate,\n} from './scorer-gate';\n\nexport {\n  DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE,\n  DEFAULT_MAX_LENGTH,\n  DEFAULT_RERANK_DTYPE,\n  FAST_RERANKER_MODEL,\n  LOCAL_RERANKER_MODEL,\n  ORT_SESSION_OPTIONS,\n  activeExecutionTarget,\n  loadCrossEncoder,\n  localRerankAvailable,\n  rerankExecutionHealth,\n  scoreCrossEncoder,\n  scoreCrossEncoderInline,\n  type LocalRerankOptions,\n  type RerankExecutionHealth,\n} from './local-engine';\n\nexport {\n  getRerankWorkerState,\n  scoreViaWorker,\n  shutdownLocalReranker,\n  type ScoreViaWorkerRequest,\n} from './local-reranker-worker';\n\nexport {\n  CPU_EXECUTION_TARGET,\n  CUDA_EXECUTION_TARGET,\n  RERANK_DEVICE_ENV,\n  WEBGPU_EXECUTION_TARGET,\n  demotedTarget,\n  executionTargetFor,\n  isCoherentTarget,\n  resolveExecutionTarget,\n  type RerankDevice,\n  type RerankExecutionTarget,\n} from './execution-target';\n\nexport {\n  DEFAULT_SIDECAR_MAX_ATTEMPTS,\n  DEFAULT_SIDECAR_TIMEOUT_MS,\n  RERANK_SIDECAR_URL_ENV,\n  SIDECAR_MAX_TEXT_CHARS,\n  SidecarRerankHttpError,\n  buildSidecarFirstReranker,\n  isNonRetryableSidecarError,\n  resolveRerankSidecarUrl,\n  sidecarRerankBatch,\n  type RerankScoreFn,\n  type SidecarFirstRerankerOpts,\n  type SidecarRerankResponse,\n} from './sidecar-reranker';\n\nexport interface RerankDoc<T> {\n  /** Stable id (for caching / debugging). */\n  id: string;\n  /** The text the reranker scores against the query (e.g. product title). */\n  text: string;\n  /** Caller's payload, carried through untouched. */\n  row: T;\n}\n\n/** Which cross-encoder does the scoring. Default `zeroentropy`. */\nexport type RerankEngine = 'zeroentropy' | 'local';\n\nexport interface RerankOptions extends LocalRerankOptions {\n  /**\n   * Scoring engine. `local` runs ONNX in-process (no key, no network);\n   * `zeroentropy` calls the hosted zerank API. Default `zeroentropy` — callers\n   * opt in to local, so an existing consumer's behavior is unchanged.\n   */\n  engine?: RerankEngine;\n  /** Model id. Engine-specific: a zerank model, or an HF cross-encoder repo id. */\n  model?: string;\n  /** API key (hosted engine only). Default process.env.ZEROENTROPY_API_KEY. */\n  apiKey?: string;\n  /** Return only the top N after reranking. Default: all. */\n  topN?: number;\n  /**\n   * Drop results below this relevance score. Meaningful because both engines\n   * emit a 0..1 score (zerank's is calibrated; the local engine squashes its\n   * logit through a sigmoid) — unlike uncalibrated vector distances.\n   *\n   * ⚠ Absolute thresholds are DTYPE-SPECIFIC on the local engine: quantization\n   * preserves ordering but compresses the score range, so a floor fitted on\n   * fp32 rejects too much at q8. Fit it on the dtype you deploy.\n   */\n  minScore?: number;\n  /**\n   * Scoring function override for `engine: 'local'` — returns scores\n   * index-aligned with the docs, and MAY throw.\n   *\n   * This is how a sidecar-backed scorer (buildSidecarFirstReranker) reaches the\n   * ranking logic without a third engine branch: whatever it throws is caught\n   * by the SAME fail-safe seam as an in-process failure, so a sidecar outage\n   * degrades to retrieval order exactly like a missing ONNX runtime does.\n   *\n   * Typed as {@link RerankScoreFn} rather than re-declared inline, so the\n   * optional deadline argument cannot drift between the two spellings — the\n   * inline copy is what made this field silently two-arity while the exported\n   * contract had grown a third.\n   */\n  scorer?: RerankScoreFn;\n  /**\n   * Instruction for an instruction-following reranker (zerank-2). The\n   * ZeroEntropy SDK has no dedicated instruction field, so it's prepended to the\n   * query — zerank-2 reads it as ranking guidance, e.g. \"Rank the actual product\n   * the shopper wants above parts/accessories for it.\" Default: none.\n   *\n   * IGNORED by the `local` engine: a plain cross-encoder is trained on\n   * (query, passage) pairs and injecting instruction prose into the query\n   * degrades its scoring rather than steering it.\n   */\n  instruction?: string;\n  /**\n   * Wall-clock bound on SCORING. On expiry the rerank degrades through the\n   * SAME fail-safe passthrough as any other scoring failure — it never throws\n   * and never stalls the caller. Default {@link DEFAULT_RERANK_TIMEOUT_MS};\n   * `0`/`Infinity` disables it.\n   *\n   * ⚠ This is a BACKSTOP against a hang, deliberately NOT a UX budget. It sits\n   * ABOVE the sidecar client's own 15s retry budget (DEFAULT_SIDECAR_TIMEOUT_MS)\n   * so it can never pre-empt that retry policy and convert a recoverable blip\n   * into a silent degradation. A user-facing caller wanting search-grade\n   * latency must pass its OWN, much tighter value — the right bound depends on\n   * the caller's latency contract, which this library cannot know.\n   *\n   * The losing promise is not cancellable (neither ONNX inference nor an\n   * in-flight fetch aborts here), so it runs to completion in the background\n   * and its result is discarded; a late rejection is swallowed rather than\n   * surfacing as an unhandled rejection after we have already degraded.\n   */\n  timeoutMs?: number;\n  /**\n   * Called EXACTLY ONCE, and only when this call fell through to the fail-safe\n   * passthrough — i.e. the returned rows are the INPUT order with\n   * `reranked: false`. Never called on a successful rerank.\n   *\n   * WHY IT EXISTS (WI-37670). The passthrough is the whole point of this\n   * library's fail-safe contract, but it is byte-identical to what a\n   * rerank-DISABLED caller produces, so from the outside a degraded stage and a\n   * healthy stage that simply found nothing to reorder look the same. A caller\n   * measuring the reranker's effect (an A/B, a bench, a scorecard) then reads a\n   * confident +0.000 and concludes \"reranking does not help\" — which happened,\n   * and had to be retracted. Reporting WHY the passthrough fired is what lets a\n   * caller void the reading instead of publishing it.\n   */\n  onDegrade?: (reason: RerankDegradeReason) => void;\n}\n\n/**\n * Why a rerank call fell through to the fail-safe passthrough.\n *\n * These mean OPPOSITE things operationally and must not be collapsed:\n * `empty-input` is benign; `timeout` says the stage was too slow for the\n * caller's budget (raise the budget, cut the candidate count, or reduce\n * in-flight concurrency — one serialized inference thread multiplies every\n * concurrent call's wall clock); `scoring-failed` says the engine could not\n * score at all (missing credential, unavailable runtime, a scorer that threw,\n * or a length mismatch); `no-usable-scores` says it scored but nothing survived\n * shaping (`minScore`/`topN`).\n */\nexport type RerankDegradeReason = 'empty-input' | 'timeout' | 'scoring-failed' | 'no-usable-scores';\n\nexport interface RerankResult<T> {\n  /** Caller's payload, carried through untouched. */\n  row: T;\n  /** Relevance score (0..1), or 0 when reranking was skipped. */\n  score: number;\n  /** True when the score came from the reranker (vs. a fail-safe passthrough). */\n  reranked: boolean;\n}\n\n/**\n * What every engine returns: scores index-aligned with the input docs.\n * - `null`      → the engine could not score at all; fail-safe passthrough.\n * - `undefined` at index i → this doc was not scored, and is dropped.\n */\ntype EngineScores = Array<number | undefined> | null;\n\nlet _client: ZeroEntropy | null = null;\nlet _clientKey: string | null = null;\nfunction getClient(apiKey: string): ZeroEntropy {\n  if (!_client || _clientKey !== apiKey) {\n    _client = new ZeroEntropy({ apiKey });\n    _clientKey = apiKey;\n  }\n  return _client;\n}\n\n/**\n * True if reranking is configured.\n *\n * The `local` engine needs no credential, so it is always configured — pass the\n * options object to ask about a specific engine. The legacy string form\n * (`rerankAvailable(apiKey)`) still asks the hosted-engine question.\n */\nexport function rerankAvailable(optsOrApiKey?: string | RerankOptions): boolean {\n  const opts: RerankOptions = typeof optsOrApiKey === 'string' ? { apiKey: optsOrApiKey } : (optsOrApiKey ?? {});\n  if (opts.engine === 'local') return true;\n  return !!(opts.apiKey ?? process.env.ZEROENTROPY_API_KEY);\n}\n\n/** Hosted zerank. Returns index-aligned scores, or null to trigger passthrough. */\nasync function zeroEntropyScores<T>(\n  query: string,\n  docs: Array<RerankDoc<T>>,\n  opts: RerankOptions,\n): Promise<EngineScores> {\n  const apiKey = opts.apiKey ?? process.env.ZEROENTROPY_API_KEY;\n  if (!apiKey) return null;\n\n  try {\n    const res = await getClient(apiKey).models.rerank({\n      model: opts.model ?? 'zerank-2',\n      // zerank-2 instruction-following format (per ZeroEntropy docs): the\n      // instruction is embedded in the query via XML tags, NOT a free-text prefix.\n      query: opts.instruction ? `<query>${query}</query>\\n<instruction>${opts.instruction}</instruction>` : query,\n      documents: docs.map((d) => d.text),\n    });\n    const scores: Array<number | undefined> = new Array(docs.length).fill(undefined);\n    for (const r of (res.results ?? []) as Array<{ index: number; relevance_score: number }>) {\n      // Out-of-range indices from the API are dropped, not crashed on.\n      if (docs[r.index] !== undefined) scores[r.index] = r.relevance_score;\n    }\n    return scores;\n  } catch {\n    return null;\n  }\n}\n\n/** Local cross-encoder — in-process by default, or an injected `scorer` (e.g.\n *  the sidecar client). Returns index-aligned scores, or null to fail safe. */\nasync function localScores<T>(\n  query: string,\n  docs: Array<RerankDoc<T>>,\n  opts: RerankOptions,\n): Promise<EngineScores | typeof SCORE_TIMEOUT> {\n  const texts = docs.map((d) => d.text);\n  if (!opts.scorer) {\n    // Deliberately NOT `localEngineScores`, which collapses every failure into\n    // the same `null`. A deadline failure — including an admission SHED, where\n    // the shared scorer refused the job at ~0ms because it provably could not\n    // finish in time — must reach the caller as `timeout`, not `scoring-failed`:\n    // those two call for opposite responses, which is the whole reason\n    // `onDegrade` names them separately (WI-37670). The fail-safe itself is\n    // unchanged; only the reason is now preserved.\n    try {\n      return await scoreCrossEncoder(query, texts, opts);\n    } catch (err) {\n      return isDeadlineFailure(err) ? SCORE_TIMEOUT : null;\n    }\n  }\n  try {\n    // Forward the deadline: the production wiring ALWAYS takes this branch (the\n    // operator injects a sidecar-first scorer), and with no sidecar that scorer\n    // is the in-process cross-encoder. Omitting it here would leave the shipped\n    // desktop path — the only one with the defect — still unbounded.\n    // The third argument is passed ONLY when there is a deadline to pass, so a\n    // scorer (or a test spy) that expects the original two-arg shape sees it\n    // unchanged.\n    const scores =\n      opts.deadline === undefined\n        ? await opts.scorer(query, texts)\n        : await opts.scorer(query, texts, { deadline: opts.deadline });\n    // A length mismatch would misalign every score with its document, so treat\n    // it as a failure rather than ranking on garbage.\n    if (!Array.isArray(scores) || scores.length !== texts.length) return null;\n    return scores.map((s) => (typeof s === 'number' && Number.isFinite(s) ? s : undefined));\n  } catch (err) {\n    // Same distinction as the branch above: an injected scorer (the sidecar\n    // client, whose own fallback is the in-process engine) can surface a\n    // deadline failure, and that is a budget verdict rather than an outage.\n    return isDeadlineFailure(err) ? SCORE_TIMEOUT : null;\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Reorder `docs` by cross-encoder relevance to `query`. Returns results sorted\n * best-first. On a missing credential, an unavailable engine, or any error,\n * returns `docs` in original order (reranked=false) so callers can always use\n * the result safely.\n */\n/**\n * Backstop bound on scoring (ms). Deliberately ABOVE the sidecar client's own\n * 15s retry budget so it never truncates that retry policy — this catches a\n * genuine HANG (a wedged in-process engine, a scorer that never settles), not\n * a slow-but-progressing rerank. Callers with a latency contract (a user-facing\n * search route) pass their own, tighter `timeoutMs`.\n */\nexport const DEFAULT_RERANK_TIMEOUT_MS = 20_000;\n\n/** Distinguishes \"the timer won\" from a legitimate `null` scoring result. */\nconst SCORE_TIMEOUT = Symbol('rerank-score-timeout');\n\n/**\n * Resolve `scores`, or the {@link SCORE_TIMEOUT} sentinel if `timeoutMs` elapses\n * first. Both still take the SINGLE fail-safe passthrough in {@link rerank} —\n * the sentinel exists only so the passthrough can NAME which of the two fired,\n * because \"too slow for your budget\" and \"the engine cannot score\" call for\n * opposite responses from the caller.\n */\nasync function withScoreTimeout<S>(\n  scores: Promise<S>,\n  timeoutMs: number,\n): Promise<S | typeof SCORE_TIMEOUT> {\n  if (!Number.isFinite(timeoutMs) || timeoutMs <= 0) return scores;\n\n  // The race loser keeps running (inference/fetch are not cancellable here). If\n  // it later REJECTS with nobody awaiting it, Node reports an unhandled\n  // rejection — attach the sink now, before racing, so there is no window.\n  scores.catch(() => {});\n\n  let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined;\n  try {\n    const winner = await Promise.race([\n      scores,\n      new Promise<typeof SCORE_TIMEOUT>((resolve) => {\n        timer = setTimeout(() => resolve(SCORE_TIMEOUT), timeoutMs);\n      }),\n    ]);\n    return winner;\n  } finally {\n    // Always clear: a surviving timer would hold the event loop open for up to\n    // timeoutMs after a fast rerank already returned.\n    if (timer !== undefined) clearTimeout(timer);\n  }\n}\n\nexport async function rerank<T>(\n  query: string,\n  docs: Array<RerankDoc<T>>,\n  opts: RerankOptions = {},\n): Promise<Array<RerankResult<T>>> {\n  // Every fail-safe passthrough NAMES its reason: a caller measuring the\n  // reranker's effect cannot otherwise tell a degrade from a null result.\n  const passthrough = (reason: RerankDegradeReason): Array<RerankResult<T>> => {\n    opts.onDegrade?.(reason);\n    return docs.slice(0, opts.topN ?? docs.length).map((d) => ({ row: d.row, score: 0, reranked: false }));\n  };\n\n  if (!query.trim() || docs.length === 0) return passthrough('empty-input');\n\n  const timeoutMs = opts.timeoutMs ?? DEFAULT_RERANK_TIMEOUT_MS;\n\n  // Give the in-process engine the SAME instant the race is measuring against,\n  // so it can stop scoring rather than run on unwatched after we degrade. The\n  // race alone cannot do this: its loser is not cancellable. Only the local\n  // engine is ours to stop — a hosted HTTP call is bounded by its own client,\n  // and an injected `scorer` belongs to the caller.\n  const scoringOpts: RerankOptions =\n    opts.engine === 'local' && Number.isFinite(timeoutMs) && timeoutMs > 0 && opts.deadline === undefined\n      ? { ...opts, deadline: Date.now() + timeoutMs }\n      : opts;\n\n  const scores = await withScoreTimeout(\n    opts.engine === 'local'\n      ? localScores(query, docs, scoringOpts)\n      : zeroEntropyScores(query, docs, scoringOpts),\n    timeoutMs,\n  );\n  if (scores === SCORE_TIMEOUT) return passthrough('timeout');\n  if (!scores) return passthrough('scoring-failed');\n\n  let ordered = docs\n    .map((d, i) => ({ row: d.row, score: scores[i], reranked: true }))\n    .filter((r): r is { row: T; score: number; reranked: true } => typeof r.score === 'number')\n    // Descending by score. Array.prototype.sort is stable, so equal scores keep\n    // their retrieval order — the right tiebreak, since retrieval order already\n    // encodes the first-stage ranking.\n    .sort((a, b) => b.score - a.score);\n\n  if (typeof opts.minScore === 'number') ordered = ordered.filter((r) => r.score >= opts.minScore!);\n  if (typeof opts.topN === 'number') ordered = ordered.slice(0, opts.topN);\n  // Guard: if shaping left nothing usable, fall back rather than drop results.\n  return ordered.length > 0 ? ordered : passthrough('no-usable-scores');\n}\n"
          },

          "repository": "libs/generic/memory",
          "repositoryRevision": "fe9878936d3da86d872fc1a5fdd29877e903d1f0",
          "path": "src/sidecar-embedder.ts",
          "gitBlob": "f4df564acaa54415b14b59b3a7ab41969b447937",
          "sha256": "6aa17f449b4fe25ac09da37ce77dc77070f0c0fb091e6d72a31bf9c312b9a092",
          "bytes": 19360,
          "text": "/**\n * Sidecar-first embedder client (P-003, plan\n * shared-embedding-sidecar-and-enrichment-2026-07-10; sidecar-REQUIRED since\n * WI-4021, owner directive 2026-07-11).\n *\n * The consumer-side seam for the shared embedding sidecar: an EmbedFn over the\n * loopback sidecar (D-004 wire — POST {url}/embed { model, kind, texts }).\n *\n * AVAILABILITY CONTRACT (v2 — D-003 retired): when a sidecar URL is\n * configured, the sidecar is REQUIRED. A failure is retried briefly (the\n * sidecar is systemd-supervised with Restart=always, so a crash window is\n * seconds) and then THROWN — never silently absorbed by an in-process model\n * load. The old D-003 in-process failover let a stalling sidecar drag every\n * embedding host into duplicate in-process model loads (the 2026-07-11\n * \"mem0 down\" flap incident) and hid sidecar sickness instead of surfacing\n * it; memory writes survive a real outage via the write-ahead journal\n * (memory-write-journal-auto-recovery-2026-07-11), reads fail loudly.\n *\n * The caller-supplied in-process builder is used ONLY when NO sidecar is\n * configured (url null — desktop installs, tests, bench rigs): there it is\n * the sole engine, not a fallback. Vectors are BIT-IDENTICAL either way\n * (D-002): the sidecar wraps the SAME @papercusp/memory builders (model,\n * prompts, MRL truncation, ORT runtime) — same space on every path.\n *\n * Retry shape: one total `timeoutMs` budget (default 15s — a freshly\n * restarted sidecar may still be warm-loading) spans ALL attempts, so a\n * slow-but-alive sidecar is never hammered past its budget; fast failures\n * (connect refused during a restart) get up to `maxAttempts` tries with short\n * linear backoff inside that budget.\n *\n * Plain `fetch`, zero new dependencies — this library is deliberately dep-free\n * (pg only); the server lives in operator-core, never here.\n */\n\nimport type { GemmaEmbedKind } from './gemma-embedder';\n\ntype EmbedFn = (text: string, signal?: AbortSignal) => Promise<number[]>;\n\n/** Consumers point at a sidecar by setting this (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:3384). */\nexport const EMBED_SIDECAR_URL_ENV = 'PAPERCUSP_EMBED_SIDECAR_URL';\n\n/** The sidecar base URL this process should use, or null when none is\n *  configured (→ pure in-process embedding). */\nexport function resolveEmbedSidecarUrl(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = process.env): string | null {\n  const url = env[EMBED_SIDECAR_URL_ENV]?.trim();\n  return url ? url.replace(/\\/$/, '') : null;\n}\n\nexport interface SidecarEmbedBatchOpts {\n  model: string;\n  kind: GemmaEmbedKind;\n  texts: string[];\n  /** Evaluate inference directly rather than the sidecar's cache. */\n  bypassCache?: boolean;\n  timeoutMs?: number;\n  /** Optional caller lifetime. Aborting it closes the HTTP request immediately\n   *  instead of leaving stale work in the shared sidecar FIFO until the\n   *  client's independent timeout expires. */\n  signal?: AbortSignal;\n  fetchFn?: typeof fetch;\n}\n\nexport interface SidecarEmbedResponse {\n  vectors: number[][];\n  dims: number;\n  runtime: string;\n  modelRev: string;\n  cache?: { hits: number; coalesced: number; inferred: number };\n}\n\nexport const DEFAULT_SIDECAR_TIMEOUT_MS = 15_000;\n\n/**\n * Per-text allowance added on top of the base budget for a BATCH embed.\n *\n * WHY A BATCH CANNOT INHERIT THE SINGLE-EMBED DEFAULT (EI-19464574865993243):\n * `DEFAULT_SIDECAR_TIMEOUT_MS` is a budget for ONE embed. `sidecarEmbedBatch`\n * accepts `texts[]`, so a caller that omits `timeoutMs` silently gives N texts\n * the deadline sized for one — and every real caller omitted it. Measured\n * 2026-08-03 on papercup-bg-host: `embedBatchSize` is 128 on a server-tier box\n * and the observed throughput is ~0.22s/text, so a full batch needs ~28s and\n * was being aborted at 15s on EVERY sweep for hours. The AbortController fires,\n * fetch rejects with \"This operation was aborted\", and embed-backfill falls back\n * to the per-row path — same rows embedded, same success counts, just ~N× slower.\n *\n * The failure is HARDWARE-TIERED, which is why it hid: a laptop profile batches\n * 32 (~7s, fits in 15s) and works fine. The bigger the box, the more certainly\n * the batch optimization disables itself — it broke exactly where it was meant\n * to pay off.\n *\n * 2s/text is deliberately conservative after WI-2146713's 2026-09-06 live\n * probe: 16 unique 2,000-character gemma/document texts reached the model\n * (cache hits 0) and completed in 34.4s. That makes the old 30s n=16 budget a\n * false-abort path. The ceiling exists to catch a SICK sidecar, not to pace a\n * healthy one, and a false abort here costs the entire batch optimization.\n * Erring long is the cheap direction.\n */\nexport const SIDECAR_BATCH_PER_TEXT_MS = 2_000;\n\n/** Absolute ceiling for a batch budget, so a huge `texts[]` cannot produce an\n *  effectively unbounded request. */\nexport const SIDECAR_BATCH_TIMEOUT_CAP_MS = 180_000;\n\n/**\n * The default budget for a batch of `textCount` texts. Exported so a caller\n * that also imposes its OWN outer bound can derive it from the SAME number\n * instead of picking a second one — two independently-chosen deadlines where\n * the tighter silently wins is precisely how this bug survived: embed-backfill\n * wrapped the batch in a deliberate 90s race, which could never fire, because\n * this client aborted it at 15s first.\n */\nexport function sidecarBatchTimeoutMs(textCount: number): number {\n  const scaled = DEFAULT_SIDECAR_TIMEOUT_MS + SIDECAR_BATCH_PER_TEXT_MS * Math.max(0, textCount - 1);\n  return Math.min(SIDECAR_BATCH_TIMEOUT_CAP_MS, scaled);\n}\n/** Attempts per embed when the sidecar is required (fast failures only — the\n *  shared `timeoutMs` budget caps total wall time regardless). */\nexport const DEFAULT_SIDECAR_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3;\n\n/** The sidecar server's own per-text char cap (embed-sidecar-server.ts\n *  MAX_TEXT_CHARS — kept in sync here since the client, not the server, is\n *  the one place every embed caller funnels through). A text over this limit\n *  is truncated client-side BEFORE it is ever sent (EI-14101): the sidecar's\n *  own 400 for this condition says \"truncate before embedding\", so truncating\n *  at the ONE shared client seam means no individual caller (embed-backfill,\n *  write-journal, memory writes, …) has to reimplement the cap. */\nexport const SIDECAR_MAX_TEXT_CHARS = 32_000;\n\n/** Thrown by sidecarEmbedBatch on a non-2xx sidecar response. Carries the\n *  HTTP status so a retry policy can tell a DETERMINISTIC client-side\n *  rejection (4xx — the exact same request can never succeed on retry) apart\n *  from a transient server/network failure (5xx, connect refused, timeout) —\n *  see isNonRetryableSidecarError. */\nexport class SidecarEmbedHttpError extends Error {\n  readonly status: number;\n  constructor(status: number, detail: string) {\n    super(`sidecar_embed_${status}: ${detail}`);\n    this.name = 'SidecarEmbedHttpError';\n    this.status = status;\n  }\n}\n\n/** True for a sidecar failure that retrying can never fix (a 4xx: the\n *  sidecar looked at THIS request and rejected it — bad shape, unknown\n *  model, oversized text pre-truncation, …). False for anything else\n *  (network/connect/timeout/5xx), which IS worth a bounded retry — the\n *  sidecar may just be mid-restart. */\nexport function isNonRetryableSidecarError(e: unknown): boolean {\n  return e instanceof SidecarEmbedHttpError && e.status >= 400 && e.status < 500;\n}\n\n/**\n * One D-004 wire call. Throws on ANY failure (network, timeout, non-200,\n * malformed/mismatched response) — callers own the fallback decision.\n * Exported for batch consumers (embed-backfill, P-004) that want the\n * texts[] amortization the single-text EmbedFn seam can't express.\n *\n * Texts over SIDECAR_MAX_TEXT_CHARS are truncated before submission (the\n * sidecar rejects them outright otherwise — a deterministic 400 that no\n * amount of retrying would fix).\n */\nexport async function sidecarEmbedBatch(url: string, opts: SidecarEmbedBatchOpts): Promise<SidecarEmbedResponse> {\n  const fetchFn = opts.fetchFn ?? fetch;\n  const texts = opts.texts.map((t) => (t.length > SIDECAR_MAX_TEXT_CHARS ? t.slice(0, SIDECAR_MAX_TEXT_CHARS) : t));\n  // Scales with the batch: the single-embed default aborts a full batch mid-flight\n  // and every caller omitted `timeoutMs` (EI-19464574865993243).\n  const timeoutMs = opts.timeoutMs ?? sidecarBatchTimeoutMs(texts.length);\n  const ctl = new AbortController();\n  const timer = setTimeout(() => ctl.abort(), timeoutMs);\n  const abortFromCaller = (): void => ctl.abort(opts.signal?.reason);\n  if (opts.signal?.aborted) abortFromCaller();\n  else opts.signal?.addEventListener('abort', abortFromCaller, { once: true });\n  try {\n    const res = await fetchFn(`${url.replace(/\\/$/, '')}/embed`, {\n      method: 'POST',\n      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },\n      body: JSON.stringify({ model: opts.model, kind: opts.kind, texts,\n        ...(opts.bypassCache === undefined ? {} : { bypassCache: opts.bypassCache }) }),\n      signal: ctl.signal,\n    });\n    if (!res.ok) {\n      const detail = await res.text().catch(() => '');\n      throw new SidecarEmbedHttpError(res.status, detail.slice(0, 200));\n    }\n    const body = (await res.json()) as SidecarEmbedResponse;\n    if (\n      !Array.isArray(body.vectors) ||\n      body.vectors.length !== texts.length ||\n      body.vectors.some((v) => !Array.isArray(v) || v.length === 0 || typeof v[0] !== 'number')\n    ) {\n      throw new Error('sidecar_embed_bad_shape: vectors missing/mismatched');\n    }\n    return body;\n  } finally {\n    clearTimeout(timer);\n    opts.signal?.removeEventListener('abort', abortFromCaller);\n  }\n}\n\nexport interface SidecarFirstEmbedderOpts {\n  /** Sidecar-side model name ('gemma' | 'local' | 'harrier'). */\n  model: string;\n  /** Asymmetric task side — the sidecar owns the actual prompt text (D-004). */\n  kind: GemmaEmbedKind;\n  /** Lazy builder for the in-process embedder — used ONLY when no sidecar is\n   *  configured (url null AND no ensure hook), where it is the sole engine.\n   *  When a url or an ensure hook is set it is never built: the sidecar is\n   *  required (WI-4021, D-003 retired). */\n  fallback: () => EmbedFn | Promise<EmbedFn>;\n  /** Sidecar base URL; defaults to resolveEmbedSidecarUrl(). null/absent ⇒\n   *  pure in-process, unless `ensure` is set (see there). */\n  url?: string | null;\n  /** TOTAL budget per embed across every attempt (default 15s). */\n  timeoutMs?: number;\n  /** Attempts within the budget on sidecar failure (default 3). */\n  maxAttempts?: number;\n  fetchFn?: typeof fetch;\n  /** Clock seam for tests. */\n  now?: () => number;\n  /** Backoff-sleep seam for tests. */\n  sleepFn?: (ms: number) => Promise<void>;\n  /** Down/up/rejected transition logging seam (default console.warn,\n   *  transition-only).         {
          "repository": "libs/generic/rerank",
          "repositoryRevision": "40e78e06b07a94203e151a44979394acc2dbc871",
          "path": "src/sidecar-reranker.ts",
          "gitBlob": "7e9d79ec39396063a25a4ee10d1a1bb85cb4b9b9",
          "sha256": "359fdd2b4d5dc851ba4d0d906049ffbca6934773e678e233aec240a1599c94d9",
          "bytes": 22554,
          "text": "/**\n * Sidecar-first reranker client — the consumer side of the shared sidecar's\n * `POST {url}/rerank` wire.\n *\n * AVAILABILITY CONTRACT — deliberately identical to the embedder's\n * (`@papercusp/memory` sidecar-embedder.ts, sidecar-REQUIRED since WI-4021):\n * when a sidecar URL is configured the sidecar is REQUIRED. A failure is\n * retried briefly inside ONE total budget and then THROWN — never silently\n * absorbed by loading an in-process model. Silent failover is what let a\n * stalling sidecar drag every host into duplicate model loads and hid sidecar\n * sickness instead of surfacing it. The in-process engine is used ONLY when NO\n * sidecar is configured (desktop installs, tests, bench rigs), where it is the\n * sole engine rather than a fallback.\n *\n * ⚠ Throwing here does NOT make search brittle, and the two behaviours are not\n * in tension: this client throws so sidecar sickness is VISIBLE, and the lib's\n * single fail-safe seam one layer up (`localEngineScores` → `rerank`'s\n * passthrough) converts that throw into \"keep retrieval order\". So a rerank\n * outage still degrades rather than breaking search — it just stops being\n * invisible on the way.\n *\n * Same sidecar PROCESS as the embedder, so it is the same env var and the same\n * base URL — a host runs one sidecar serving both /embed and /rerank.\n *\n * Plain `fetch`, no new dependencies.\n *\n * ⚠ The retry/budget/transition POLICY below intentionally mirrors\n * sidecar-embedder.ts line for line. It is duplicated rather than shared\n * because these are two independently-borrowable libs and neither may depend\n * on the other. If you change the policy here, change it there too — and see\n * EI-19310953148940030, which proposes extracting it once a third client\n * appears (each bullet of that policy is a bug someone already paid for, so a\n * one-sided fix is the real risk).\n */\n\nimport { LOCAL_RERANKER_MODEL, scoreCrossEncoder, type LocalRerankOptions } from './local-engine';\nimport { RerankDeadlineError, isDeadlineFailure } from './scorer-gate';\n\n/**\n * Per-call scoring controls. Optional so that every existing\n * `(query, texts) => …` scorer still satisfies {@link RerankScoreFn} unchanged.\n */\nexport interface RerankScoreCallOpts {\n  /**\n   * Absolute epoch-ms instant after which scoring should STOP.\n   *\n   * Honoured by both engines. The in-process engine uses it to stop scoring\n   * after the caller has degraded; the sidecar path uses it for admission and\n   * for the HTTP attempt budget. Without this, concurrent callers can queue\n   * behind the sidecar's serialized scorer and then all abort together, while\n   * the client incorrectly reports a healthy-but-busy sidecar as down.\n   */\n  deadline?: number;\n}\n\n/** Scores `texts` against `query`, index-aligned. Throws on failure. */\nexport type RerankScoreFn = (\n  query: string,\n  texts: string[],\n  opts?: RerankScoreCallOpts,\n) => Promise<number[]>;\n\n/** The SAME env var the embedder uses — one sidecar process serves both. */\nexport const RERANK_SIDECAR_URL_ENV = 'PAPERCUSP_EMBED_SIDECAR_URL';\n\n/** The sidecar base URL this process should use, or null when none is\n *  configured (→ pure in-process reranking). */\nexport function resolveRerankSidecarUrl(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = process.env): string | null {\n  const url = env[RERANK_SIDECAR_URL_ENV]?.trim();\n  return url ? url.replace(/\\/$/, '') : null;\n}\n\nexport const DEFAULT_SIDECAR_TIMEOUT_MS = 15_000;\n/** Attempts per call when the sidecar is required (fast failures only — the\n *  shared `timeoutMs` budget caps total wall time regardless). */\nexport const DEFAULT_SIDECAR_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3;\n\n/** Kept in sync with the sidecar server's own per-text cap. Truncating at this\n *  ONE client seam means no individual caller has to reimplement it, and the\n *  server's 400 for an oversized text becomes unreachable in practice. */\nexport const SIDECAR_MAX_TEXT_CHARS = 32_000;\n\nexport interface SidecarRerankResponse {\n  scores: number[];\n  runtime: string;\n  modelRev: string;\n}\n\n/** Thrown on a non-2xx sidecar response. Carries the HTTP status so a retry\n *  policy can tell a DETERMINISTIC client-side rejection (4xx — this exact\n *  request can never succeed) apart from a transient failure (5xx, connect\n *  refused, timeout). */\nexport class SidecarRerankHttpError extends Error {\n  readonly status: number;\n  constructor(status: number, detail: string) {\n    super(`sidecar_rerank_${status}: ${detail}`);\n    this.name = 'SidecarRerankHttpError';\n    this.status = status;\n  }\n}\n\n/** True for a failure retrying can never fix (a 4xx). False for anything else\n *  (network/connect/timeout/5xx), which IS worth a bounded retry. */\nexport function isNonRetryableSidecarError(e: unknown): boolean {\n  return e instanceof SidecarRerankHttpError && e.status >= 400 && e.status < 500;\n}\n\nexport interface SidecarRerankBatchOpts {\n  model: string;\n  query: string;\n  texts: string[];\n  timeoutMs?: number;\n  fetchFn?: typeof fetch;\n}\n\n/**\n * One wire call. Throws on ANY failure (network, timeout, non-200, malformed\n * or mis-sized response) — callers own the retry/fallback decision.\n */\nexport async function sidecarRerankBatch(url: string, opts: SidecarRerankBatchOpts): Promise<SidecarRerankResponse> {\n  const fetchFn = opts.fetchFn ?? fetch;\n  const timeoutMs = opts.timeoutMs ?? DEFAULT_SIDECAR_TIMEOUT_MS;\n  const texts = opts.texts.map((t) => (t.length > SIDECAR_MAX_TEXT_CHARS ? t.slice(0, SIDECAR_MAX_TEXT_CHARS) : t));\n  const query =\n    opts.query.length > SIDECAR_MAX_TEXT_CHARS ? opts.query.slice(0, SIDECAR_MAX_TEXT_CHARS) : opts.query;\n  const ctl = new AbortController();\n  const timer = setTimeout(() => ctl.abort(), timeoutMs);\n  try {\n    const res = await fetchFn(`${url.replace(/\\/$/, '')}/rerank`, {\n      method: 'POST',\n      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },\n      body: JSON.stringify({ model: opts.model, query, texts }),\n      signal: ctl.signal,\n    });\n    if (!res.ok) {\n      const detail = await res.text().catch(() => '');\n      throw new SidecarRerankHttpError(res.status, detail.slice(0, 200));\n    }\n    const body = (await res.json()) as SidecarRerankResponse;\n    // A length mismatch would silently misalign every score with its document,\n    // producing a plausible-looking but wrong ordering — reject it loudly.\n    if (\n      !Array.isArray(body.scores) ||\n      body.scores.length !== texts.length ||\n      body.scores.some((s) => typeof s !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(s))\n    ) {\n      throw new Error('sidecar_rerank_bad_shape: scores missing/mismatched');\n    }\n    return body;\n  } finally {\n    clearTimeout(timer);\n  }\n}\n\ninterface SidecarAdmissionEntry {\n  pairs: number;\n  deadline: number;\n  run: () => Promise<unknown>;\n  resolve: (value: unknown) => void;\n  reject: (reason?: unknown) => void;\n}\n\ninterface SidecarAdmissionGate {\n  enqueue<T>(pairs: number, deadline: number, run: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T>;\n}\n\n/**\n * The sidecar's default scorer is one serialized inference resource. A\n * per-scorer HTTP queue keeps concurrent callers from piling whole batches\n * into the server FIFO. Recent observations of the SAME batch size can shed\n * a call before it opens a socket. HTTP latency includes fixed queue/ensure\n * costs, so it cannot be divided by pair count and extrapolated to an unseen\n * batch size. Expired observations are unknown, allowing a bounded new sample.\n * This is deliberately a separate gate from scorer-gate.ts:\n * the latter protects local CPU, while this one protects the remote sidecar.\n */\nfunction createSidecarAdmissionGate(now: () => number): SidecarAdmissionGate {\n  let active = false;\n  const waiting: SidecarAdmissionEntry[] = [];\n  const batchCosts = new Map<number, { elapsedMs: number; measuredAt: number }>();\n\n  const deadlineError = (entry: SidecarAdmissionEntry, remaining: number, predictedMs: number | null): Error =>\n    new RerankDeadlineError(\n      `rerank: scoring deadline exceeded before sidecar dispatch for ${entry.pairs} pairs — ` +\n        `the sidecar queue needs ~${predictedMs ?? 'unknown'}ms but only ${Math.max(0, Math.round(remaining))}ms remain; ` +\n        'shedding now rather than labeling a healthy sidecar as down',\n    );\n\n  const pump = (): void => {\n    if (active) return;\n    const entry = waiting.shift();\n    if (!entry) return;\n\n    const instant = now();\n    const remaining = entry.deadline - instant;\n    for (const [pairs, cost] of batchCosts) {\n      if (instant - cost.measuredAt >= DEFAULT_SIDECAR_TIMEOUT_MS) batchCosts.delete(pairs);\n    }\n    const observed = batchCosts.get(entry.pairs);\n    const predictedMs = observed ? Math.ceil(observed.elapsedMs) : null;\n    if (remaining <= 0 || (predictedMs !== null && predictedMs > remaining)) {\n      entry.reject(deadlineError(entry, remaining, predictedMs));\n      // A queue can contain several calls whose deadlines have already\n      // expired. Drain those synchronously instead of leaving them to be\n      // mistaken for sidecar failures on a later wake.\n      pump();\n      return;\n    }\n\n    active = true;\n    const startedAt = now();\n    let completed = false;\n    void Promise.resolve()\n      .then(() => entry.run())\n      .then(\n        (value) => {\n          completed = true;\n          entry.resolve(value);\n        },\n        (err) => entry.reject(err),\n      )\n      .finally(() => {\n        if (completed) {\n          const elapsed = Math.max(0, now() - startedAt);\n          if (elapsed > 0 && entry.pairs > 0) {\n            const prior = batchCosts.get(entry.pairs);\n            batchCosts.set(entry.pairs, { elapsedMs: prior ? prior.elapsedMs * 0.3 + elapsed * 0.7 : elapsed,\n              measuredAt: now() });\n            // Bound bookkeeping even for clients with unusual batch sizes.\n            if (batchCosts.size > 128) batchCosts.delete(batchCosts.keys().next().value!);\n          }\n        }\n        active = false;\n        pump();\n      });\n  };\n\n  return {\n    enqueue<T>(pairs: number, deadline: number, run: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {\n      return new Promise<T>((resolve, reject) => {\n        waiting.push({\n          pairs,\n          deadline,\n          run,\n          resolve: (value) => resolve(value as T),\n          reject,\n        });\n        pump();\n      });\n    },\n  };\n}\n\n/**\n * Every operator-side scorer normally shares one builder, but keep the gate\n * shared even when a bench or a test creates several clients. The weak keys\n * avoid retaining custom fetch/clock seams after their caller is gone, while\n * the production `fetch`/`Date.now` pair gives all clients for one sidecar a\n * single admission lane.\n */\nconst sidecarAdmissionGates = new Map<string, WeakMap<object, WeakMap<object, SidecarAdmissionGate>>>();\n\nfunction sidecarAdmissionGateFor(\n  url: string,\n  model: string,\n  fetchFn: typeof fetch,\n  now: () => number,\n): SidecarAdmissionGate {\n  const key = `${url}\\0${model}`;\n  let byFetch = sidecarAdmissionGates.get(key);\n  if (!byFetch) {\n    byFetch = new WeakMap<object, WeakMap<object, SidecarAdmissionGate>>();\n    sidecarAdmissionGates.set(key, byFetch);\n  }\n  const fetchKey = fetchFn as unknown as object;\n  let byClock = byFetch.get(fetchKey);\n  if (!byClock) {\n    byClock = new WeakMap<object, SidecarAdmissionGate>();\n    byFetch.set(fetchKey, byClock);\n  }\n  const clockKey = now as unknown as object;\n  let gate = byClock.get(clockKey);\n  if (!gate) {\n    gate = createSidecarAdmissionGate(now);\n    byClock.set(clockKey, gate);\n  }\n  return gate;\n}\n\nexport interface SidecarFirstRerankerOpts {\n  /** Host observation seam for the configured in-process scorer. */\n  observeFallback?: LocalRerankOptions['observeFallback'];\n  /** Sidecar-side model name ('rerank' | 'rerank-fast'). */\n  model?: string;\n  /** In-process model id, used only when no sidecar is configured. */\n  localModel?: string;\n  /** In-process dtype, used only when no sidecar is configured. */\n  dtype?: string;\n  /** Sidecar base URL; defaults to resolveRerankSidecarUrl(). null/absent ⇒\n   *  pure in-process, unless `ensure` is set (see there). */\n  url?: string | null;\n  /** Explicit TOTAL sidecar cap per call across every attempt. When omitted,\n   * the caller's absolute deadline owns the budget; 15s is the fallback only\n   * when neither caller nor client supplies a budget. An explicit cap still\n   * wins over a longer caller deadline. */\n  timeoutMs?: number;\n  /** Attempts within the budget on sidecar failure (default 3). */\n  maxAttempts?: number;\n  fetchFn?: typeof fetch;\n  /** Clock seam for tests. */\n  now?: () => number;\n  /** Backoff-sleep seam for tests. */\n  sleepFn?: (ms: number) => Promise<void>;\n  /** In-process scorer seam (tests inject; default is the local ONNX engine). */\n  localScorer?: RerankScoreFn;\n  /** Down/up/rejected transition logging seam (transition-only, so a sustained\n   *  outage logs once rather than per call). 'rejected' = the sidecar is UP and\n   *  correctly refusing a bad request — distinct from 'down' so the log never\n   *  claims unavailability when the sidecar is fine. */\n  onTransition?: (state: 'down' | 'up' | 'rejected', detail: string) => void;\n  /** Re-establish the sidecar before each attempt. A sidecar this process\n   *  spawned may have exited after an idle period, and this hook re-launches\n   *  it on demand.           "repository": "libs/generic/rerank",
          "repositoryRevision": "40e78e06b07a94203e151a44979394acc2dbc871",
          "path": "src/local-engine.ts",
          "gitBlob": "fc3dad4ae91c448b87c0222800a98788f9afb7a2",
          "sha256": "0d175f7d3e8206454626fa2ce614e69d040e3ac5ebbdf094fd3694b9bc61877d",
          "bytes": 25500,
          "text": "/**\n * Local ONNX cross-encoder engine for @papercusp/rerank.\n *\n * The lib's original engine calls a hosted API (ZeroEntropy zerank). This one\n * runs the cross-encoder IN-PROCESS via Transformers.js/ONNX Runtime, so\n * reranking costs no API key, no network hop, and no per-call spend — which is\n * what makes it usable on every search, not just the ones someone paid for.\n *\n * Contract: identical to every other engine here — index-aligned scores, and\n * `null` for \"I could not score this\" so the caller degrades to retrieval order\n * rather than breaking search. Nothing in this file may throw to its caller.\n *\n * Model shape it expects: a sequence-classification cross-encoder that emits\n * ONE logit per (query, doc) pair — `ModernBertForSequenceClassification` with\n * num_labels=1, e.g. `Alibaba-NLP/gte-reranker-modernbert-base`. Two-label\n * cross-encoders are also handled (softmax, take the \"relevant\" class), so the\n * engine is not welded to one architecture.\n *\n * Deliberately NOT here (they belong to later plan items, not to the engine):\n * an HTTP sidecar with one warm model per host, and host-aware dtype selection.\n * This file only has to be correct and fail-safe in-process.\n */\n\nimport {\n  CPU_EXECUTION_TARGET,\n  type RerankDevice,\n  type RerankExecutionTarget,\n  demotedTarget,\n  resolveExecutionTarget,\n} from './execution-target';\nimport { getRerankWorkerState, scoreViaWorker, warnRerankFallback } from './local-reranker-worker';\nimport { isDeadlineFailure, runInScorerGate } from './scorer-gate';\n\n/** Cross-encoder that emits one logit per pair. num_labels=1, ModernBERT. */\nexport const LOCAL_RERANKER_MODEL = 'Alibaba-NLP/gte-reranker-modernbert-base';\n\n/**\n * Fast tier: ~7.5x cheaper per pair (23M params / 6 layers vs 149M), at a real\n * quality cost. Measured, not assumed — see the plan's D-001. Use it where the\n * candidate pool is large or the latency budget is tight.\n */\nexport const FAST_RERANKER_MODEL = 'Xenova/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2';\n\n/**\n * ONNX Runtime defaults intraOp threads to EVERY core and spin-waits them — on\n * a many-core host that grows a huge spin pool per loading process and stutters\n * the whole box (the same trap the local embedder hit, WI-3792). Cap it.\n *\n * Capping costs us nothing here: D-001 MEASURED that cross-encoder latency on\n * this workload does not improve with more cores (4 pinned cores matched a\n * 128-core box), so per-pair cost is bounded by the candidate cap, not by\n * threads. Kept identical to the embedder's cap so the two can share a host.\n */\nexport const ORT_SESSION_OPTIONS = { intraOpNumThreads: 4, interOpNumThreads: 1 } as const;\n\n/**\n * q8 is the CPU-correct default, MEASURED rather than assumed (plan D-006): on\n * 4 pinned cores it is 1.60x faster per pair than fp32 and never changed the\n * top result (top-1 agreement 1.000 across 6 queries, NDCG@5 0.9855).\n *\n * fp16/q4f16 are GPU formats. On the CPU provider fp16 is not merely slower —\n * the graph FAILS TO INITIALISE outright (ORT's precision-free-cast insertion\n * breaks on ModernBERT's SimplifiedLayerNormFusion), so the engine's fail-safe\n * would silently drop reranking entirely. That is why dtype is chosen as a PAIR\n * with the execution provider; see `execution-target.ts`.\n *\n * Prefer `resolveExecutionTarget()` over this constant — it is retained for the\n * callers that legitimately pin a dtype (tests, benchmarks).\n */\nexport const DEFAULT_RERANK_DTYPE = 'q8';\n\n/** Pairs are truncated to this many tokens. The model supports 8192, but a\n *  cross-encoder's cost is superlinear in sequence length and a reranker scores\n *  a match-centred passage, not a whole document — 512 is the useful window. */\nexport const DEFAULT_MAX_LENGTH = 512;\n\n/** Pairs per forward pass. Padding is to the longest member of the batch, so a\n *  huge batch wastes compute on padding; 16 keeps memory flat and padding cheap. */\nexport const DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE = 16;\n\nexport interface LocalRerankOptions {\n  /** Optional domain-free host sink for actual device and worker decisions. */\n  observeFallback?: (mechanism: string, decision: { eligible: number; applied: number; reason: string }) => unknown;\n  /** HF model id. Default `LOCAL_RERANKER_MODEL`. */\n  model?: string;\n  /**\n   * ONNX weight format. Defaults WITH `device` as a coherent pair (see\n   * `execution-target.ts`) — do not set this alone unless you mean to: `fp16`\n   * without a GPU `device` is not a slow configuration, it is an unloadable one.\n   */\n  dtype?: string;\n  /**\n   * ONNX Runtime execution provider. Defaults WITH `dtype` as a pair. Passing a\n   * GPU device does not force it: the engine verifies the session actually\n   * constructs and falls back to the whole CPU pair if it does not.\n   */\n  device?: RerankDevice;\n  /** Truncate each (query, doc) pair to this many tokens. Default 512. */\n  maxLength?: number;\n  /** Pairs per forward pass. Default 16. */\n  batchSize?: number;\n  /**\n   * Absolute epoch-ms instant after which scoring STOPS, checked between\n   * batches. Throws on expiry, which `localEngineScores` converts to the same\n   * fail-safe `null` as any other scoring failure — so an over-budget rerank\n   * degrades to retrieval order rather than running to completion unwatched.\n   *\n   * Distinct from the caller's `timeoutMs` and NOT a replacement for it. That\n   * one bounds how long the CALLER waits; this one stops the WORK. Both are\n   * needed because the losing side of a `Promise.race` is not cancellable: with\n   * only the race, an abandoned rerank keeps burning a core for the rest of its\n   * natural life, on the very host (no sidecar ⇒ in-process) least able to\n   * spare one. `rerank()` derives this from `timeoutMs` automatically.\n   */\n  deadline?: number;\n}\n\n// --- Minimal structural types for the optional dependency ------------------\n// Typed structurally rather than imported, so this lib does not take a hard\n// build-time dependency on @huggingface/transformers.\n\ninterface LogitsTensor {\n  dims: number[];\n  data: ArrayLike<number>;\n}\ntype Tokenizer = (\n  text: string[],\n  opts: { text_pair: string[]; padding: boolean; truncation: boolean; max_length: number },\n) => Record<string, unknown>;\ntype SequenceClassifier = (inputs: Record<string, unknown>) => Promise<{ logits: LogitsTensor }>;\n\ninterface TransformersModule {\n  AutoTokenizer: { from_pretrained(model: string, opts?: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<Tokenizer> };\n  AutoModelForSequenceClassification: {\n    from_pretrained(model: string, opts?: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<SequenceClassifier>;\n  };\n}\n\nconst TRANSFORMERS_PACKAGE = '@huggingface/transformers';\n\n// Keep the optional dependency lazy and opaque to bundlers through a runtime\n// specifier. Native import retains the host callback in VM module runners;\n// new Function loses it and falsely reports an installed engine unavailable.\n// This is the native-import leg of memory's existing optional-import seam,\n// kept local so this standalone library does not depend on the memory stack.\nasync function dynamicImport<T>(specifier: string): Promise<T> {\n  return (await import(/* @vite-ignore */ specifier)) as T;\n}\n\ninterface LoadedModel {\n  tokenizer: Tokenizer;\n  model: SequenceClassifier;\n}\n\n/** One warm model per (id, dtype). Loading is seconds; scoring is milliseconds,\n *  so the cache is the difference between usable and unusable. */\nconst _models = new Map<string, Promise<LoadedModel>>();\n\n/** Injected in tests so the engine's own logic is testable without ONNX. */\nlet _loaderOverride: ((model: string, dtype: string, device: RerankDevice) => Promise<LoadedModel>) | null =\n  null;\n\n/**\n * Test-only: permit the WORKER path even while a loader override is installed.\n *\n * Normally an injected loader forces the inline path (it is an in-process object\n * and cannot cross a thread boundary). That rule makes the worker→inline\n * FALLBACK unreachable from tests, because the override short-circuits before\n * the worker is ever tried — so this seam exists purely to exercise \"the worker\n * failed, did we degrade correctly?\" against a fake model. Production never\n * installs a loader override, so this combination cannot occur outside tests.\n */\nlet _workerWithLoaderForTest = false;\nexport function _setWorkerWithLoaderForTest(enabled: boolean): void {\n  _workerWithLoaderForTest = enabled;\n}\n\nasync function defaultLoader(model: string, dtype: string, device: RerankDevice): Promise<LoadedModel> {\n  const transformers = await dynamicImport<TransformersModule>(TRANSFORMERS_PACKAGE);\n  const [tokenizer, classifier] = await Promise.all([\n    transformers.AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model),\n    transformers.AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained(model, {\n      dtype,\n      device,\n      session_options: ORT_SESSION_OPTIONS,\n    }),\n  ]);\n  return { tokenizer, model: classifier };\n}\n\n/**\n * Load (and cache) the cross-encoder. Exported so a warm-model host can preload\n * it at startup instead of paying the load on a user's first search.\n *\n * Rejects on failure — and de-caches, so a transient failure (a half-downloaded\n * model, a cold network) does not poison the process for its whole lifetime.\n */\nexport function loadCrossEncoder(opts: LocalRerankOptions = {}): Promise<LoadedModel> {\n  return loadOnTarget(opts.model ?? LOCAL_RERANKER_MODEL, effectiveTarget(opts), opts.observeFallback);\n}\n\n/**\n * Resolve the (device, dtype) PAIR for a call.\n *\n * The pair is the unit: when the caller says nothing we take the host's whole\n * target, never one field from the host and one from a constant. An explicit\n * `dtype`/`device` is still honoured (tests and experiments need to pin one),\n * but it can only ever narrow a coherent starting point — it cannot silently\n * produce `fp16` on the CPU provider by defaulting the other half.\n */\nfunction effectiveTarget(opts: LocalRerankOptions): RerankExecutionTarget {\n  const host = resolveExecutionTarget();\n  if (opts.device === undefined && opts.dtype === undefined) return host;\n  const device = opts.device ?? host.device;\n  const dtype = opts.dtype ?? host.dtype;\n  return { device, dtype, why: 'explicit caller override' };\n}\n\n/**\n * Has the GPU target been proven to work on this host? A GPU that is present is\n * not a GPU that is usable — the CUDA provider fails to load without cuDNN, and\n * the fp16 graph fails to initialise on the CPU provider. We therefore find out\n * by CONSTRUCTING a session, and remember the answer so a broken GPU host pays\n * the failed load once rather than on every search.\n */\nlet _gpuUnusable = false;\n\n/**\n * The demotion itself, REMEMBERED rather than only logged.\n *\n * A `console.warn` fires once per process and is then gone: it cannot be read\n * by a health check, a test, or an operator asking \"why is search slow?\" three\n * weeks later. Keeping the verdict here is what lets `activeExecutionTarget()`\n * and `rerankExecutionHealth()` distinguish a demoted host from a deliberate\n * CPU one — see `demotedTarget` for why that distinction is load-bearing.\n */\nlet _demotion: { from: RerankExecutionTarget; cause: string; target: RerankExecutionTarget } | null =\n  null;\n\n/** Reported once per process when a GPU target is demoted, so the fallback is\n *  visible in a log instead of silently costing quality. */\nfunction reportDemotion(target: RerankExecutionTarget, err: unknown, observeFallback?: LocalRerankOptions['observeFallback']): void {\n  try { observeFallback?.('rerank-device', { eligible: 1, applied: 0, reason: 'gpu-construction-failed' }); } catch { /* no-throw sink */ }\n  const cause = String((err as Error)?.message ?? err).slice(0, 200);\n  _demotion = { from: target, cause, target: demotedTarget(target, cause) };\n  console.warn(\n    `[rerank] ${target.device}/${target.dtype} session failed to construct — falling back to ` +\n      `${CPU_EXECUTION_TARGET.device}/${CPU_EXECUTION_TARGET.dtype}. ` +\n      `Reranking continues on CPU. Cause: ${cause}`,\n  );\n}\n\n/**\n * Load on `target`, falling back to the CPU PAIR — both fields together — if a\n * non-CPU target cannot construct a session.\n *\n * Falling back on `device` alone would leave `dtype: 'fp16'` pointed at the CPU\n * provider, which is the single worst configuration available and is exactly\n * what a naive \"GPU didn't work, use the CPU\" retry produces.\n */\nfunction loadOnTarget(model: string, target: RerankExecutionTarget, observeFallback?: LocalRerankOptions['observeFallback']): Promise<LoadedModel> {\n  const effective = target.device !== 'cpu' && _gpuUnusable ? CPU_EXECUTION_TARGET : target;\n  if (target.device !== 'cpu' && _gpuUnusable) {\n    try { observeFallback?.('rerank-device', { eligible: 1, applied: 0, reason: 'sticky-gpu-demotion' }); } catch { /* no-throw sink */ }\n  }\n  const key = `${model}::${effective.dtype}::${effective.device}`;\n\n  const cached = _models.get(key);\n  if (cached) return cached;\n\n  const loading = (_loaderOverride ?? defaultLoader)(model, effective.dtype, effective.device).then((loaded) => {\n    if (effective.device !== 'cpu') {\n      try { observeFallback?.('rerank-device', { eligible: 1, applied: 1, reason: 'applied' }); } catch { /* no-throw sink */ }\n    }\n    return loaded;\n  }).catch(\n    (err) => {\n      _models.delete(key);\n      if (effective.device === 'cpu') throw err;\n      // Demote the WHOLE pair, once, then retry on CPU.\n      _gpuUnusable = true;\n      reportDemotion(effective, err, observeFallback);\n      return loadOnTarget(model, CPU_EXECUTION_TARGET);\n    },\n  );\n  _models.set(key, loading);\n  return loading;\n}\n\n/** The pair this host will actually run on, after any verified demotion. Exposed\n *  so a warm-model host / health check can REPORT the real configuration rather\n *  than the requested one. */\nexport function activeExecutionTarget(): RerankExecutionTarget {\n  const host = resolveExecutionTarget();\n  if (host.device === 'cpu' || !_gpuUnusable) return host;\n  // Report the DEMOTED pair, not the bare CPU constant: same device/dtype, but a\n  // `why` that says a GPU was asked for and refused. Falling back to the plain\n  // constant here is what made a degraded host unreadable from a healthy one.\n  return _demotion?.target ?? CPU_EXECUTION_TARGET;\n}\n\n/**\n * Requested vs actual execution target, and whether the gap is a demotion.\n *\n * `activeExecutionTarget()` alone answers \"what is running\"; it cannot answer\n * \"is that what we asked for?\" without the caller separately resolving the host\n * target and comparing — which nothing in this repo did, so a GPU host that\n * quietly reverted to CPU looked exactly like a CPU host. This returns both\n * sides plus the verdict, so the comparison cannot be forgotten.\n *\n * `demoted: false` before the first load is HONEST, not a clean bill: the GPU\n * session is only verified by constructing one. Read it after a load.\n */\nexport interface RerankExecutionHealth {\n  /** What this host asked for (`PAPERCUSP_RERANK_DEVICE`). */\n  requested: RerankExecutionTarget;\n  /** What it will actually run on, after any verified demotion. */\n  active: RerankExecutionTarget;\n  /** True once a requested GPU target has failed to construct a session. */\n  demoted: boolean;\n  /** The construction error that forced the demotion; null when not demoted. */\n  demotionCause: string | null;\n}\n\nexport function rerankExecutionHealth(): RerankExecutionHealth {\n  return {\n    requested: resolveExecutionTarget(),\n    active: activeExecutionTarget(),\n    demoted: _demotion !== null,\n    demotionCause: _demotion?.cause ?? null,\n  };\n}\n\nconst sigmoid = (x: number): number => 1 / (1 + Math.exp(-x));\n\n/**\n * Collapse a row of logits to one relevance score.\n *\n * - 1 logit  → sigmoid. The single-logit cross-encoder convention.\n * - N logits → softmax, take class 1 (\"relevant\" by the binary cross-encoder\n *   convention). Only the 0/1 pair matters, so softmax over those two is both\n *   correct for N=2 and a sane reading for N>2.\n *\n * Both are MONOTONIC in the underlying logit, so ordering is unaffected by the\n * squashing — which matters because ordering is the only thing quantization\n * preserves exactly (D-001: q8 keeps the ranking but compresses the score\n * range, so any absolute threshold must be fitted on the deployed dtype).\n */\nfunction scoreFromLogits(row: number[]): number {\n  if (row.length === 1) return sigmoid(row[0]);\n  const [negative, positive] = row;\n  return sigmoid(positive - negative);\n}\n\n/**\n * Hand the event loop a turn.\n *\n * `setImmediate` fires in the CHECK phase, which the loop reaches only after\n * passing through the TIMERS phase — so this is what lets an armed `setTimeout`\n * (every wall-clock bound in this lib is one) actually run. `await`-ing an\n * already-resolved promise would NOT do it: that only queues a microtask, and\n * the microtask queue is drained to empty before the loop advances a phase, so\n * a loop of `await` over synchronous work starves timers exactly as a bare\n * `while` loop would. That distinction IS the bug this yield fixes.\n *\n * Falls back to `setTimeout(0)` where `setImmediate` is absent (browser/worker\n * builds); this lib is deliberately environment-agnostic.\n */\nfunction yieldToEventLoop(): Promise<void> {\n  return new Promise<void>((resolve) => {\n    if (typeof setImmediate === 'function') setImmediate(resolve);\n    else setTimeout(resolve, 0);\n  });\n}\n\n/**\n * Score every (query, text) pair. Returns scores index-aligned with `texts`.\n *\n * Throws on load/inference failure — the fail-safe conversion to \"return the\n * input order untouched\" happens in the engine wrapper below, so a caller that\n * wants to SEE the failure (a warm-up probe, a health check, the sidecar) can.\n *\n * ⚠ COOPERATIVE WHEN INLINE (EI-20005411672741677). A cross-encoder forward pass\n * is CPU-bound and holds the thread, so while it runs on the MAIN thread nothing\n * else in this process makes progress — including the `setTimeout` behind every\n * one of this lib's wall-clock bounds. A timer cannot preempt it; there is no\n * third option between \"the work yields\" and \"the work runs elsewhere\". So the\n * inline loop yields between batches and re-checks its deadline there, bounding\n * the caller's wait to at most ONE batch of overrun instead of the whole stage.\n *\n * The preferred path takes the third option: `scoreCrossEncoder` dispatches to a\n * WORKER THREAD (`local-reranker-worker.ts`, WI-37555), which makes the caller's\n * bound EXACT rather than bounded-to-one-batch. This inline function remains the\n * fallback for hosts where a worker cannot spawn — degraded, never broken.\n */\nexport async function scoreCrossEncoderInline(\n  query: string,\n  texts: string[],\n  opts: LocalRerankOptions = {},\n): Promise<number[]> {\n  if (texts.length === 0) return [];\n\n  const { tokenizer, model } = await loadCrossEncoder(opts);\n  const maxLength = opts.maxLength ?? DEFAULT_MAX_LENGTH;\n  const batchSize = Math.max(1, opts.batchSize ??           "bytes": 9054,
          "text": "/**\n * Deadline-aware admission control for the shared in-process cross-encoder.\n *\n * WHY (WI-37676). Every wall-clock bound in this library is PER-CALL, but the\n * in-process scorer is ONE shared resource. Measured on this box 2026-08-10,\n * over the real worker path, at 24 and at 100 pairs:\n *\n *     concurrency   1      2      4      8\n *     per-call     1.00x  2.04x  3.98x  7.68x   (of the solo wall clock)\n *     throughput   30.9   30.3   31.1   32.2    pairs/s\n *\n * Per-call latency is EXACTLY linear in the number of callers, and aggregate\n * throughput is flat. Two consequences, and the second is the whole point:\n *\n *  1. Concurrency buys NOTHING here. Admitting N callers at once does not\n *     finish the work sooner; it only spreads the same completion time over\n *     everyone. So serializing costs no throughput.\n *  2. Un-admitted concurrency makes failure CORRELATED. Once N exceeds\n *     budget/solo (~5 at the shipped 4s bound), every in-flight call blows its\n *     budget at roughly the same moment and the whole stage degrades at once —\n *     after each caller has spent its entire budget waiting. Nobody gets a\n *     reranked page and the CPU was burned producing none.\n *\n * This gate turns that into the strictly better outcome: callers that CAN make\n * their budget run one after another and succeed; a caller that provably cannot\n * is shed IMMEDIATELY, at ~0ms, with the same fail-safe passthrough it would\n * have reached the slow way. It gets the identical page, several seconds sooner.\n *\n * ⚠ SAFETY ARGUMENT FOR THE ESTIMATOR. The shed decision rests on a measured\n * cost estimate, which can be wrong in both directions — and neither direction\n * is worse than the status quo, which is what makes this safe to default ON:\n *  - over-shed  ⇒ a call that would have just squeaked in returns retrieval\n *                 order EARLY. Same rows, same order as the timeout it replaces.\n *  - under-shed ⇒ the call proceeds and may time out. Exactly today's behaviour.\n * The gate can therefore only move latency down and the success count up; it\n * cannot invent a failure that did not already exist.\n *\n * NOT for the sidecar's HTTP leg. This gates in-process scoring only — the\n * shared CPU. A sidecar call is someone else's capacity with its own retry\n * budget, and throttling it here would be throttling the wrong resource.\n */\n\n/**\n * A scoring attempt abandoned because it could not meet its caller's deadline.\n *\n * Shaped to match the message the engine and the worker already throw, so the\n * existing `/deadline exceeded/` handling in `scoreCrossEncoder` — \"this is a\n * real verdict, do NOT retry it inline\" — applies to a shed unchanged. Retrying\n * a shed inline would burn the very budget that just proved insufficient, on the\n * main thread.\n */\nexport class RerankDeadlineError extends Error {\n  constructor(message: string) {\n    super(message);\n    this.name = 'RerankDeadlineError';\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Did this failure mean \"too slow for your budget\" rather than \"could not score\"?\n *\n * Message matching is not laziness: the worker's throw crosses a thread\n * boundary, where a structured-clone of an Error keeps `message` and loses the\n * prototype, so `instanceof` is unavailable on exactly the path that matters\n * most. The class check is kept for the in-process throws it does work for.\n */\nexport function isDeadlineFailure(err: unknown): boolean {\n  if (err instanceof RerankDeadlineError) return true;\n  return err instanceof Error && /deadline exceeded/.test(err.message);\n}\n\n/** Env override for hosts where scoring genuinely parallelizes (a GPU target). */\nexport const RERANK_MAX_CONCURRENT_ENV = 'RERANK_MAX_CONCURRENT_SCORERS';\n\ninterface Waiter {\n  pairs: number;\n  deadline: number | undefined;\n  admit: () => void;\n  refuse: (err: Error) => void;\n}\n\nlet _maxConcurrent: number | null = null;\nlet _active = 0;\nlet _activePairs = 0;\nconst _queue: Waiter[] = [];\n\n/**\n * Exponentially-weighted mean ms per (query, doc) pair, measured from this\n * process's own completed jobs. `null` until calibrated — and while it is null\n * the gate NEVER sheds, because a shed decision taken from a guess is a made-up\n * failure. Serialization still applies; only the shedding waits for evidence.\n */\nlet _msPerPair: number | null = null;\nlet _observations = 0;\n\nfunction maxConcurrent(): number {\n  if (_maxConcurrent !== null) return _maxConcurrent;\n  const raw = Number(process.env[RERANK_MAX_CONCURRENT_ENV]);\n  _maxConcurrent = Number.isFinite(raw) && raw >= 1 ? Math.floor(raw) : 1;\n  return _maxConcurrent;\n}\n\n/**\n * Cost of everything that must finish before a newly-arriving job of `pairs`\n * pairs could complete, in ms. Uses TOTAL pairs of in-flight work as an upper\n * bound on what remains: a job halfway done is charged as if it had not started.\n * That errs toward shedding, which is the harmless direction (see the header).\n */\nfunction estimatedWaitMs(pairs: number): number | null {\n  if (_msPerPair === null) return null;\n  const backlog = _activePairs + _queue.reduce((n, w) => n + w.pairs, 0);\n  return (backlog + pairs) * _msPerPair;\n}\n\nfunction wouldMissDeadline(pairs: number, deadline: number | undefined): boolean {\n  if (deadline === undefined) return false;\n  const wait = estimatedWaitMs(pairs);\n  if (wait === null) return false;\n  return Date.now() + wait > deadline;\n}\n\nfunction shedError(pairs: number, deadline: number): RerankDeadlineError {\n  const wait = Math.round(estimatedWaitMs(pairs) ?? 0);\n  const budget = Math.max(0, deadline - Date.now());\n  return new RerankDeadlineError(\n    `rerank: scoring deadline exceeded after 0 of ${pairs} pairs — the shared scorer is ` +\n      `${_active} deep with ${_queue.length} queued, so this call needs ~${wait}ms against ` +\n      `${budget}ms of budget. Shedding now rather than spending the budget waiting.`,\n  );\n}\n\n/** Drain as many queued callers as the concurrency limit allows. */\nfunction pump(): void {\n  while (_queue.length > 0 && _active < maxConcurrent()) {\n    const w = _queue.shift()!;\n    // Re-check AT THE HEAD, not only on arrival: a caller admitted to the queue\n    // when the backlog was short can become undeliverable while it waits, and\n    // starting it then would spend a budget already known to be insufficient.\n    if (w.deadline !== undefined && wouldMissDeadline(w.pairs, w.deadline)) {\n      w.refuse(shedError(w.pairs, w.deadline));\n      continue;\n    }\n    _active++;\n    _activePairs += w.pairs;\n    w.admit();\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Run `fn` under the gate. Rejects with a {@link RerankDeadlineError} — without\n * ever calling `fn` — when the shared scorer provably cannot deliver in time.\n */\nexport async function runInScorerGate<T>(\n  pairs: number,\n  deadline: number | undefined,\n  fn: () => Promise<T>,\n): Promise<T> {\n  if (pairs <= 0) return await fn();\n\n  if (deadline !== undefined && wouldMissDeadline(pairs, deadline)) {\n    throw shedError(pairs, deadline);\n  }\n\n  await new Promise<void>((admit, refuse) => {\n    _queue.push({ pairs, deadline, admit, refuse });\n    pump();\n  });\n\n  const startedAt = Date.now();\n  const soloRun = _active === 1;\n  try {\n    return await fn();\n  } finally {\n    const elapsed = Date.now() - startedAt;\n    _active--;\n    _activePairs -= pairs;\n    // Calibrate only from a job that had the scorer to ITSELF — otherwise the\n    // sample measures contention, not cost, and the estimator would inflate\n    // under exactly the load it is meant to reason about.\n    //\n    // The FIRST observation is dropped: it pays this process's one-time model\n    // load (~1.2s here), which is not a per-pair cost and would otherwise seed\n    // the estimator an order of magnitude high and shed everything after it.\n    if (soloRun && elapsed > 0) {\n      _observations++;\n      if (_observations > 1) {\n        const sample = elapsed / pairs;\n        _msPerPair = _msPerPair === null ? sample : _msPerPair * 0.7 + sample * 0.3;\n      }\n    }\n    pump();\n  }\n}\n\n/** Diagnostics; also the seam the tests assert the invariants through. */\nexport function getScorerGateState(): {\n  active: number;\n  queued: number;\n  maxConcurrent: number;\n  msPerPair: number | null;\n  observations: number;\n} {\n  return {\n    active: _active,\n    queued: _queue.length,\n    maxConcurrent: maxConcurrent(),\n    msPerPair: _msPerPair,\n    observations: _observations,\n  };\n}\n\n/** Test seam: set the calibration directly instead of measuring it. */\nexport function _setScorerGateCalibrationForTest(msPerPair: number | null, observations = 2): void {\n  _msPerPair = msPerPair;\n  _observations = observations;\n}\n\n/** Test seam: override the concurrency limit (`null` ⇒ re-read the env). */\nexport function _setScorerGateConcurrencyForTest(n: number | null): void {\n  _maxConcurrent = n;\n}\n\n/** Test seam — same function under the codebase's `_reset*` convention. */\nexport function _resetScorerGateForTest(): void {\n  _maxConcurrent = null;\n  _active = 0;\n  _activePairs = 0;\n  _queue.length = 0;\n  _msPerPair = null;\n  _observations = 0;\n}\n",

          "text": "/**\n * Host-aware execution target for the local cross-encoder (plan P-009).\n *\n * ## The one rule this file exists to enforce\n *\n * **dtype is not independently selectable — it is a property of the DEVICE.**\n * A weight format and an execution provider are chosen TOGETHER or not at all,\n * because the wrong half of the pair is worse than either whole:\n *\n * - `fp16` is a GPU format. x86 has no native fp16 compute, so ONNX Runtime's\n *   CPU provider casts every fp16 weight up to fp32 at inference time and pays\n *   the conversion on top of full-precision math. MEASURED on this stack, not\n *   assumed — see the plan's D-006.\n * - `q8` is the CPU-correct format: int8 kernels are native, the weights are ~4x\n *   smaller, and it preserves the ranking (D-006 measured top-1 agreement 1.000\n *   against fp32).\n *\n * So the selectable unit here is a `RerankExecutionTarget` — a (device, dtype)\n * PAIR — and every transition moves both fields at once. An API that let a\n * caller set `dtype: 'fp16'` while the device stayed `cpu` would make the single\n * worst configuration the easiest one to reach by accident.\n *\n * ## Why \"is there a GPU?\" is the wrong question\n *\n * Detecting a GPU is not the same as being able to USE one. The box this was\n * developed on has an RTX 3090, the CUDA 12 runtime, and ships ORT's CUDA\n * provider — and still cannot execute on it, because cuDNN 9 is absent, so\n * `libonnxruntime_providers_cuda.so` fails to load. Anything that keyed off\n * `nvidia-smi` finding a card would have selected the GPU target on that host,\n * failed to construct a session, and — because the engine is fail-safe — turned\n * every search into silent retrieval order with no reranking at all.\n *\n * Hence: the GPU target is opt-IN (`PAPERCUSP_RERANK_DEVICE`), and even when it\n * is opted into it is VERIFIED — see `local-engine.ts`, which falls back to the\n * CPU pair when a GPU session does not actually construct.\n */\n\n/** Execution providers this engine knows how to target. */\nexport type RerankDevice = 'cpu' | 'cuda' | 'webgpu';\n\nexport interface RerankExecutionTarget {\n  /** ONNX Runtime execution provider. */\n  device: RerankDevice;\n  /** ONNX weight format, valid ONLY in combination with `device`. */\n  dtype: string;\n  /** Why this pair — carried so a log line can explain itself. */\n  why: string;\n}\n\n/**\n * The safe default, and the fallback for every failed GPU attempt.\n *\n * D-006 measured on 4 pinned cores: q8 is 1.58x faster per pair than fp32 while\n * keeping top-1 agreement at 1.000 and NDCG@5 at 0.986, so it is the right CPU\n * default on quality grounds as well as cost.\n */\nexport const CPU_EXECUTION_TARGET: RerankExecutionTarget = Object.freeze({\n  device: 'cpu',\n  dtype: 'q8',\n  why: 'CPU provider: int8 kernels are native on x86, weights are ~4x smaller, and q8 preserves the ranking head (D-006)',\n});\n\n/** The GPU pair. fp16 is only ever correct WITH a GPU execution provider. */\nexport const CUDA_EXECUTION_TARGET: RerankExecutionTarget = Object.freeze({\n  device: 'cuda',\n  dtype: 'fp16',\n  why: 'CUDA provider: fp16 is native on the GPU, halves bandwidth, and avoids the int8 quantisation error entirely',\n});\n\n/** WebGPU (desktop shell / browser). fp16 is native there too. */\nexport const WEBGPU_EXECUTION_TARGET: RerankExecutionTarget = Object.freeze({\n  device: 'webgpu',\n  dtype: 'fp16',\n  why: 'WebGPU provider: fp16 is the native shader format',\n});\n\n/**\n * The CPU pair, tagged as the outcome of a FAILED GPU attempt.\n *\n * ## Why this exists at all\n *\n * A demotion changes WHY we are on CPU, never WHICH kernels run — so `device`\n * and `dtype` are exactly `CPU_EXECUTION_TARGET`'s and every consumer that\n * branches on them is unaffected. Only `why` differs, and that difference is\n * the entire point.\n *\n * Without it, a demoted host and a deliberate CPU host render BYTE-IDENTICALLY:\n * both report `cpu`/`q8` with the \"int8 kernels are native on x86\" rationale,\n * which reads as a healthy, considered choice. That collapse is not theoretical\n * — it is why a GPU capability that was measured working (17x on this box) could\n * silently revert and go unnoticed: the engine is fail-safe, so the only symptom\n * is slowness, and the one health surface built to reveal the demotion\n * (`rerankExecution` in the embed sidecar) had no value with which to say it.\n *\n * A degraded state that is indistinguishable from the healthy state is not\n * observable, however many places report it.\n */\nexport function demotedTarget(from: RerankExecutionTarget, cause: string): RerankExecutionTarget {\n  return Object.freeze({\n    device: CPU_EXECUTION_TARGET.device,\n    dtype: CPU_EXECUTION_TARGET.dtype,\n    why:\n      `DEMOTED from ${from.device}/${from.dtype} — that session would not construct on this host, ` +\n      `so reranking is running on ${CPU_EXECUTION_TARGET.device}/${CPU_EXECUTION_TARGET.dtype} ` +\n      `(correct, but materially slower than the requested target). Cause: ${cause}`,\n  });\n}\n\n/**\n * Opt a GPU host in. Unset/`cpu` ⇒ the CPU pair; `cuda`/`webgpu` ⇒ the matching\n * GPU pair, still subject to the verified-load fallback in the engine.\n *\n * Opt-IN rather than auto-detect, deliberately: an auto-probe would pay a failed\n * multi-second model load on every CPU host, and (see the file header) presence\n * of a GPU does not imply a usable one.\n */\nexport const RERANK_DEVICE_ENV = 'PAPERCUSP_RERANK_DEVICE';\n\nconst TARGETS_BY_DEVICE: Record<RerankDevice, RerankExecutionTarget> = {\n  cpu: CPU_EXECUTION_TARGET,\n  cuda: CUDA_EXECUTION_TARGET,\n  webgpu: WEBGPU_EXECUTION_TARGET,\n};\n\n/** The pair for a device. Total over `RerankDevice`, so a new device cannot be\n *  added without also stating its dtype. */\nexport function executionTargetFor(device: RerankDevice): RerankExecutionTarget {\n  return TARGETS_BY_DEVICE[device];\n}\n\n/**\n * Resolve this host's execution target from the environment.\n *\n * Unknown/misspelled values resolve to the CPU pair rather than throwing: a typo\n * in a deployment env var must not be able to take search down, and the CPU pair\n * is always a correct answer.\n */\nexport function resolveExecutionTarget(\n  env: Record<string, string | undefined> = typeof process === 'undefined' ? {} : process.env,\n): RerankExecutionTarget {\n  const raw = (env[RERANK_DEVICE_ENV] ?? '').trim().toLowerCase();\n  if (raw === 'cuda' || raw === 'gpu') return CUDA_EXECUTION_TARGET;\n  if (raw === 'webgpu') return WEBGPU_EXECUTION_TARGET;\n  return CPU_EXECUTION_TARGET;\n}\n\n/** True when the pair is one this module vouches for. Guards the trap the whole\n *  file exists to prevent: a GPU weight format on the CPU provider. */\nexport function isCoherentTarget(target: { device: string; dtype: string }): boolean {\n  const known = TARGETS_BY_DEVICE[target.device as RerankDevice];\n  return known !== undefined && known.dtype === target.dtype;\n}\n",

          "repository": "libs/generic/rerank",
