          "path": "src/local-reranker-worker.ts",
          "gitBlob": "5b64cf164f510a6f72ce19f663e8a438c4b7e03a",
          "bytes": 20559,
          "sha256": "d58a9be8a3bf58d5f78debd24285af1253dcf7ace7118144c40a6948fe1c709f",
          "text": "/**\n * Worker-thread isolated local cross-encoder.\n *\n * WHY (EI-20005411672741677, finished by WI-37555). A cross-encoder forward pass\n * is CPU-bound and holds its thread. On the MAIN thread that means nothing else\n * in the process progresses while it runs — including the `setTimeout` behind\n * every wall-clock bound in this lib, so no timer can preempt it. `local-engine`\n * yields between batches to make those bounds REAL, but that only bounds the\n * overrun to one batch (~720ms at the default 16 pairs). With the model here,\n * the caller's `Promise.race` bound becomes EXACT — the main thread is free to\n * service its own timers — and head-of-line blocking of unrelated work goes away.\n *\n * Architecture mirrors `@papercusp/memory`'s `local-embedder-worker.ts`: one\n * persistent worker per process, lazily spawned, holding the warm model(s);\n * main-thread requests marshal a batch over `postMessage` and await a pending\n * Promise keyed by id. Falls back to inline (main-thread) scoring whenever the\n * worker is unavailable — degraded, never broken.\n */\n\nimport { pinModuleState } from '@papercusp/module-singleton';\nimport { Worker } from 'node:worker_threads';\nimport { createRequire } from 'node:module';\nimport { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';\nimport { resolve, dirname } from 'node:path';\nimport type { RerankDevice } from './execution-target';\n\ninterface PendingRequest {\n  resolve: (v: number[]) => void;\n  reject: (err: Error) => void;\n  observeFallback?: ScoreViaWorkerRequest['observeFallback'];\n}\n\ninterface WorkerState {\n  worker: Worker | null;\n  workerReady: Promise<void> | null;\n  nextId: number;\n  pending: Map<number, PendingRequest>;\n  /**\n   * Set ONLY for genuine, permanent unavailability — the worker could not be\n   * CONSTRUCTED at all (no `worker_threads`, missing script, spawn threw). A\n   * runtime crash deliberately does NOT set this: it clears the worker handle so\n   * the next call respawns one.\n   *\n   * That asymmetry is the point (the lesson EI-16184 taught the embedder path):\n   * treating a transient crash as permanent condemns every later call in the\n   * process to the inline, main-thread-blocking path — i.e. one hiccup silently\n   * undoes this whole module for the rest of the process's life.\n   */\n  workerDisabled: boolean;\n  /** Guards the process-level `beforeExit` hook so it is installed at most once,\n   *  however many times a worker (re)spawns. */\n  beforeExitHookInstalled: boolean;\n  beforeExitListener: (() => Promise<void>) | null;\n\n  /**\n   * Whether the worker is currently holding the event loop open. Mirrors the last\n   * `ref()`/`unref()` we issued, because `Worker` exposes no way to read it back.\n   */\n  refd: boolean;\n  lastFallbackWarnAt: number;\n  /** Outcome of `pinOnnxRuntimeBinding` (WI-10005090); null until the first spawn. */\n  onnxBindingPin?: OnnxBindingPin | null;\n  /** Workers detached while they owed answers, draining before terminate\n   *  (WI-10006567; mirrors the embedder's `retiring`). */\n  retiring?: Map<Worker, RetiringWorker>;\n}\n\ntype RetireOutcome = 'retired' | 'exited' | 'errored' | 'timed-out';\ninterface RetiringWorker {\n  done: Promise<void>;\n  settle: (outcome: RetireOutcome) => void;\n}\n\n/** Bound on waiting for a retiring rerank worker's in-flight scoring (WI-10006567). */\nexport const RERANK_WORKER_RETIRE_DRAIN_MS = 30_000;\n\n/** What `pinOnnxRuntimeBinding` achieved. Never thrown — reported. */\nexport type OnnxBindingPin =\n  | { status: 'pinned'; path: string }\n  | { status: 'unavailable'; reason: string }\n  | { status: 'failed'; reason: string };\n\n// tsx can evaluate this module through both CJS and ESM in one process.\n// Shutdown and health reads must see the worker started through either loader.\nconst state = pinModuleState<WorkerState>('@papercusp/rerank.local-reranker-worker', () => ({\n  worker: null, workerReady: null, nextId: 0, pending: new Map(),\n  workerDisabled: false, beforeExitHookInstalled: false, beforeExitListener: null,\n  refd: false, lastFallbackWarnAt: 0, onnxBindingPin: null,\n}));\n\nconst TRANSFORMERS_PACKAGE = '@huggingface/transformers';\n\n/**\n * Load the onnxruntime-node binding once in the spawning thread, before any\n * reranker worker loads it, and keep it for the life of the process.\n *\n * WI-10005090 (measured 2026-10-01, onnxruntime-node 1.24.3 / node 25.9): once\n * the last thread holding the binding exits, Node drops its registration while\n * the library stays mapped, so every later load in the process — a respawned\n * worker and the inline main-thread fallback — fails with \"Module did not\n * self-register\". Holding one reference keeps the registration. The embedder\n * worker (libs/generic/memory/src/local-embedder-worker.ts, same function name)\n * pins the same binding; the full measurement is documented there. Resolved\n * from the transformers package the worker script imports, so the pinned file\n * is the file the worker loads. Never throws; the first outcome stands.\n */\nexport function pinOnnxRuntimeBinding(fromPath: string): OnnxBindingPin {\n  if (!state.onnxBindingPin) state.onnxBindingPin = loadOnnxBindingFrom(fromPath);\n  return state.onnxBindingPin;\n}\n\nfunction loadOnnxBindingFrom(fromPath: string): OnnxBindingPin {\n  let transformersEntry: string;\n  try {\n    transformersEntry = createRequire(fromPath).resolve(TRANSFORMERS_PACKAGE);\n  } catch {\n    return { status: 'unavailable', reason: `${TRANSFORMERS_PACKAGE} is not resolvable from ${fromPath}` };\n  }\n  try {\n    const fromTransformers = createRequire(transformersEntry);\n    const path = fromTransformers.resolve('onnxruntime-node');\n    fromTransformers('onnxruntime-node');\n    return { status: 'pinned', path };\n  } catch (err) {\n    return { status: 'failed', reason: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err) };\n  }\n}\n\n/** The pin outcome, or null when no reranker worker has been spawned yet. */\nexport function getOnnxBindingPin(): OnnxBindingPin | null {\n  return state.onnxBindingPin ?? null;\n}\n\n/** Forget the recorded outcome (the binding stays loaded); for tests of a first-time pin. */\nexport function _resetOnnxBindingPinForTest(): void {\n  state.onnxBindingPin = null;\n}\n\n/**\n * Hold the loop open for EXACTLY as long as a request is in flight, and not one\n * moment longer.\n *\n * WHY BOTH HALVES ARE LOAD-BEARING (WI-37680). An always-ref'd worker keeps a\n * one-shot script alive forever — the bug the original `unref()` fixed. But an\n * always-UNREF'd worker is worse in a way that is silent: while the caller\n * awaits a reply, the unref'd worker (and its port) no longer count as loop\n * work, so a host with nothing else ref'd is considered IDLE **mid-request**.\n * `beforeExit` then fires, the hook below terminates the worker, and the exit\n * handler rejects the in-flight request with `rerank worker exited with code 1`\n * — which `scoreCrossEncoder` reads as \"the worker is unavailable\" and answers\n * by falling back to inline main-thread scoring.\n *\n * So the whole worker-thread mechanism silently did not apply on any host whose\n * loop is otherwise empty: every CLI, bench and one-off script. Those are\n * exactly the hosts where it was measured, which is how the inline path's\n * serialization got recorded as a property of the worker path (WI-37676).\n * Measured 2026-08-10: a `scoreViaWorker` with ZERO pairs — no model load at\n * all — failed this way 100% of the time from a standalone script.\n *\n * Ref'ing only while `state.pending` is non-empty satisfies both: a script that\n * awaits a rerank stays alive until its answer arrives, then exits naturally.\n */\nfunction syncWorkerRef(): void {\n  const want = state.pending.size > 0;\n  if (!state.worker || want === state.refd) return;\n  if (want) state.worker.ref();\n  else state.worker.unref();\n  state.refd = want;\n}\n\nfunction workerPath(): string {\n  // Co-located with this module, resolved at RUNTIME so the path survives\n  // build-time bundling — provided the build copies the script beside the\n  // bundle.           "text": "/**\n * Worker script for local-reranker-worker.ts. Runs the ONNX cross-encoder in a\n * dedicated worker_threads thread so a forward pass does not hold the Node.js\n * main event loop.\n *\n * WHY THIS EXISTS (EI-20005411672741677, finished by WI-37555). A cross-encoder\n * forward pass is CPU-bound and holds whatever thread it runs on. While it runs\n * on the MAIN thread nothing else in the process progresses — including the\n * `setTimeout` behind every one of this lib's wall-clock bounds, so a timer\n * cannot preempt it. `scoreCrossEncoder` yields between batches to make those\n * bounds real, but that only bounds the overrun to ONE batch (~720ms at the\n * default 16 pairs). Moving the model here makes the caller's `Promise.race`\n * bound EXACT, because the main thread is free to service its own timers.\n *\n * Protocol (main → worker):\n *   { kind: 'score', id: number, query: string, texts: string[],\n *     model: string, dtype: string, device: string,\n *     maxLength: number, batchSize: number, deadline?: number }\n *\n * Protocol (worker → main):\n *   { kind: 'ready' }                                   on init complete\n *   { kind: 'score_ok',  id: number, scores: number[] } on success\n *   { kind: 'score_err', id: number, error: string }    on failure\n *\n * Plain ESM .mjs because a worker_threads spawn does not go through any\n * TypeScript transform. That means the two constants below and `scoreFromLogits`\n * are DUPLICATED from local-engine.ts and must be kept in sync — the same\n * deliberate trade the local embedder's worker script already makes.\n */\n\nimport { parentPort, workerData } from 'node:worker_threads';\nimport { mkdirSync } from 'node:fs';\nimport { createRequire } from 'node:module';\nimport { homedir } from 'node:os';\nimport { dirname, join } from 'node:path';\n\n/** Mirrored from local-engine.ts — see WI-3792. ONNX Runtime otherwise grows a\n *  spin-waiting thread pool sized to EVERY core, per loading process. */\nconst ORT_SESSION_OPTIONS = { intraOpNumThreads: 4, interOpNumThreads: 1 };\n\n/** One warm model per (id, dtype, device) — loading is seconds, scoring is\n *  milliseconds, so this cache is the difference between usable and unusable. */\nconst modelsByKey = new Map();\n\n// Test seams allow a self-contained fake Transformers module and package tree;\n// production resolves the installed package from this worker script.\nconst TRANSFORMERS_SPECIFIER =\n  (workerData && typeof workerData.transformersSpecifier === 'string' && workerData.transformersSpecifier) ||\n  '@huggingface/transformers';\n\nfunction configureTransformersCache(t) {\n  const packageRoot = workerData && typeof workerData.transformersPackageRoot === 'string'\n    ? workerData.transformersPackageRoot\n    : dirname(dirname(createRequire(import.meta.url).resolve('@huggingface/transformers')));\n  const papercuspHome = process.env.PAPERCUSP_HOME || join(homedir(), '.papercusp');\n  const cacheDir = join(papercuspHome, 'cache', 'transformers');\n  mkdirSync(cacheDir, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });\n  t.env.localModelPath = join(packageRoot, '.cache');\n  t.env.cacheDir = cacheDir;\n}\n\nlet transformersPromise = null;\nfunction loadTransformers() {\n  if (!transformersPromise) {\n    transformersPromise = import(TRANSFORMERS_SPECIFIER).then((t) => {\n      configureTransformersCache(t);\n      return t;\n    });\n    transformersPromise.catch(() => {\n      transformersPromise = null;\n    });\n  }\n  return transformersPromise;\n}\n\nasync function getModel(model, dtype, device, observeFallback) {\n  const key = `${model}::${dtype}::${device}`;\n  let loaded = modelsByKey.get(key);\n  if (!loaded) {\n    // Dynamic import keeps the worker spawn cheap when @huggingface/transformers\n    // is not installed — the package only loads on the first score call.\n    loaded = loadTransformers().then(async (t) => {\n      const [tokenizer, classifier] = await Promise.all([\n        t.AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model),\n        t.AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained(model, {\n          dtype,\n          device,\n          session_options: ORT_SESSION_OPTIONS,\n        }),\n      ]);\n      return { tokenizer, model: classifier };\n    }).then((result) => {\n      if (device !== 'cpu') observeFallback({ eligible: 1, applied: 1, reason: 'applied' });\n      return result;\n    }, (error) => {\n      if (device !== 'cpu') observeFallback({ eligible: 1, applied: 0, reason: 'gpu-construction-failed' });\n      throw error;\n    });\n    modelsByKey.set(key, loaded);\n    // De-cache a failed load so a transient failure (half-downloaded model, cold\n    // network) does not poison this worker for the rest of its life.\n    loaded.catch(() => modelsByKey.delete(key));\n  }\n  return loaded;\n}\n\nconst sigmoid = (x) => 1 / (1 + Math.exp(-x));\n\n/** Mirrored from local-engine.ts. 1 logit → sigmoid; N logits → softmax over\n *  the 0/1 pair, which is `sigmoid(positive - negative)`. Both monotonic in the\n *  logit, so ordering is unaffected by the squashing. */\nfunction scoreFromLogits(row) {\n  if (row.length === 1) return sigmoid(row[0]);\n  const [negative, positive] = row;\n  return sigmoid(positive - negative);\n}\n\nasync function score(msg) {\n  const { query, texts, model, dtype, device, maxLength, batchSize, deadline } = msg;\n  if (texts.length === 0) return [];\n\n  // Check the deadline BEFORE loading, not just between batches: a model load is\n  // seconds on a cold cache, so loading first would spend the entire (already\n  // expired) budget before noticing there was none left.\n  const expired = () => deadline !== undefined && Date.now() >= deadline;\n  if (expired()) {\n    throw new Error(\n      `rerank: scoring deadline exceeded after 0 of ${texts.length} pairs — degrading to retrieval order`,\n    );\n  }\n\n  const { tokenizer, model: classifier } = await getModel(model, dtype, device, (decision) =>\n    parentPort.postMessage({ kind: 'device_decision', id: msg.id, decision }));\n  const size = Math.max(1, batchSize);\n  const scores = [];\n\n  for (let start = 0; start < texts.length; start += size) {\n    // The deadline is re-checked here as well as on the main thread. Off-thread\n    // work is not cancellable by the caller abandoning its Promise.race, so\n    // without this the worker would keep burning a core scoring a result nobody\n    // will ever read — on exactly the host (no sidecar ⇒ in-process) least able\n    // to spare one.\n    if (expired()) {\n      throw new Error(\n        `rerank: scoring deadline exceeded after ${start} of ${texts.length} pairs — degrading to retrieval order`,\n      );\n    }\n\n    const batch = texts.slice(start, start + size);\n    const inputs = tokenizer(new Array(batch.length).fill(query), {\n      text_pair: batch,\n      padding: true,\n      truncation: true,\n      max_length: maxLength,\n    });\n    const { logits } = await classifier(inputs);\n\n    const numLabels = logits.dims.length > 1 ? logits.dims[logits.dims.length - 1] : 1;\n    if (logits.data.length !== batch.length * numLabels) {\n      throw new Error(\n        `rerank: logits length ${logits.data.length} != ${batch.length} pairs x ${numLabels} labels`,\n      );\n    }\n    for (let i = 0; i < batch.length; i++) {\n      const row = [];\n      for (let l = 0; l < numLabels; l++) row.push(Number(logits.data[i * numLabels + l]));\n      scores.push(scoreFromLogits(row));\n    }\n  }\n  return scores;\n}\n\n// WI-10006567 (mirrors the embed worker): `Worker#terminate()` while an\n// onnxruntime-node run is in flight aborts the whole PROCESS (an uncatchable\n// Napi::Error -> SIGABRT). The host therefore never terminates a worker that\n// owes answers: it sends {kind:'retire'}, this thread starts no new scoring,\n// finishes what is running, and answers {kind:'retired'} once idle.\nlet retired = false;\nlet retiredAnnounced = false;\nlet inFlight = 0;\nfunction announceRetiredIfIdle() {\n  if (!retired || inFlight > 0 || retiredAnnounced) return;\n  retiredAnnounced = true;\n  parentPort.postMessage({ kind: 'retired' });\n}\n\nparentPort.on('message', async (msg) => {\n  if (!msg || typeof msg !== 'object') return;\n  if (msg.kind === 'retire') {\n    retired = true;\n    announceRetiredIfIdle();\n    return;\n  }\n  if (msg.kind !== 'score') return;\n  inFlight++;\n  try {\n    if (retired) throw new Error('rerank worker retired before this request started scoring');\n    parentPort.postMessage({ kind: 'score_ok', id: msg.id, scores: await score(msg) });\n  } catch (err) {\n    parentPort.postMessage({\n      kind: 'score_err',\n      id: msg.id,\n      error: err && err.message ? err.message : String(err),\n    });\n  } finally {\n    inFlight--;\n    announceRetiredIfIdle();\n  }\n});\n\n// Ready as soon as the handler is installed; the model loads lazily on first use.\nparentPort.postMessage({ kind: 'ready' });\n",

          "text": "{\n  \"name\": \"@papercusp/module-singleton\",\n  \"version\": \"0.1.0\",\n  \"private\": true,\n  \"type\": \"module\",\n  \"description\": \"Pin a module's mutable state to the realm under a Symbol.for key AND count module evaluations, so a split module-singleton (tsx CJS/ESM double-load, bare-vs-relative specifier, symlinked node_modules) is both fixed and observable instead of silently halving every reader's view. Domain-free; no host coupling; no dependencies.\",\n  \"main\": \"./src/index.ts\",\n  \"types\": \"./src/index.ts\",\n  \"exports\": {\n    \".\": \"./src/index.ts\"\n  },\n  \"scripts\": {\n    \"test\": \"vitest run\"\n  },\n  \"devDependencies\": {\n    \"@papercusp/test-config\": \"*\",\n    \"vitest\": \"^4.1.4\"\n  }\n}\n",

Domain-free; no host coupling; no dependencies.",
            "main": "./src/index.ts",
            "types": "./src/index.ts",

            "scripts": {

          "repository": ".",

          "path": "libs/generic/module-singleton/src/index.ts",

          "sha256": "4d8852efe38c7fddf07a77c821ba0bb704df0e52c7324182a2941db564712dbf",
          "text": "/**\n * @papercusp/module-singleton — pin a module's mutable state to the realm, and\n * COUNT how many times the module body was evaluated.\n *\n * ## The hazard\n *\n * A module that holds mutable state in module scope:\n *\n *     const registry = new Map();   // module-scoped\n *\n * is a singleton only as long as the loader produces exactly ONE module record\n * for it. Several ordinary seams break that assumption without any error:\n *\n *   - a tsx/ts-node CJS preflight alongside the ESM loader (two module systems),\n *   - the same package reached through both a bare specifier\n *     (`@scope/pkg`) and a relative path (`../pkg/src/index.ts`),\n *   - `node_modules/@scope/*` symlinked into a monorepo (two real paths),\n *   - a bundled copy living beside the source copy.\n *\n * When it splits, each module record gets its OWN `registry`, and writes to one\n * are invisible to readers of the other. Nothing throws. The symptom is a\n * *partial* view that looks like a complete one.\n *\n * ## Why counting matters as much as pinning\n *\n * Pinning the state to `globalThis` under a `Symbol.for` key fixes correctness —\n * both module records then share one object. But it also makes the duplication\n * INVISIBLE: once the state is shared, nothing distinguishes one module record\n * from two, so the underlying packaging fault is never noticed or fixed.\n *\n * This module therefore does both in one call. `pinModuleState` returns the\n * shared state (correctness) and increments an evaluation counter\n * (observability). `listModuleDuplications()` reports every key whose module body\n * ran more than once, so a split singleton can be surfaced by a health check\n * instead of being discovered days later from a contradictory reading.\n *\n * Observed live: `@papercusp/scheduled-registry` was evaluated twice inside one\n * process. A timer armed against instance A fired every 2 minutes while being\n * absent from the inventory served by instance B — in the same pid. It went\n * unnoticed for 6+ days because the surface meant to report the timers was the\n * surface that had gone blind (EI-19451658870832332 / EI-19463700807328229).\n *\n * ## Contract — call it ONCE, at module scope\n *\n *     const state = pinModuleState('@scope/pkg.state', () => ({ registry: new Map() }));\n *\n * `evaluations` counts CALLS, so this is only a module-record count when the call\n * happens exactly once per module evaluation. Calling it from a function that\n * runs repeatedly makes the count meaningless. `init` runs at most once per\n * realm; later evaluations receive the state the first one built.\n *\n * This module deliberately holds NO module-scoped state of its own — every read\n * goes through `globalThis` — so the detector cannot split the way its subjects\n * can.\n */\n\n/** A key whose module body was evaluated more than once in this realm. */\nexport interface ModuleDuplication {\n  /** The key passed to `pinModuleState`. */\n  key: string;\n  /** How many times `pinModuleState` was called for this key (>= 2 to be a duplication). */\n  evaluations: number;\n  /** Epoch ms when the first evaluation pinned the state. */\n  firstSeenAt: number;\n  /** Epoch ms of the most recent evaluation. */\n  lastSeenAt: number;\n}\n\ninterface Slot {\n  value: unknown;\n  evaluations: number;\n  firstSeenAt: number;\n  lastSeenAt: number;\n}\n\n/**\n * `Symbol.for` is the cross-realm symbol registry: a second module record\n * resolves the SAME symbol, which is exactly the property that lets two module\n * records find one store. A plain `Symbol()` would mint a distinct key per\n * evaluation and silently reintroduce the split this module exists to close.\n */\nconst SLOTS_KEY = Symbol.for('@papercusp/module-singleton.slots');\n\nfunction slots(): Map<string, Slot> {\n  const store = globalThis as unknown as Record<symbol, Map<string, Slot> | undefined>;\n  let map = store[SLOTS_KEY];\n  if (!map) {\n    map = new Map<string, Slot>();\n    store[SLOTS_KEY] = map;\n  }\n  return map;\n}\n\n/**\n * Pin a module's mutable state to the realm and record this evaluation.\n *\n * Returns the SAME object for every module record that uses `key`, so\n * module-scoped state stops being per-module-record. Call once, at module scope.\n *\n * @param key    A stable, globally unique id — use the package name plus a\n *               suffix, e.g. `'@papercusp/scheduled-registry.state'`. Two\n *               unrelated modules sharing a key would share state, so the\n *               package name is not optional decoration.\n * @param init   Builds the initial state. Runs at most once per realm.\n */\nexport function pinModuleState<T>(key: string, init: () => T): T {\n  if (typeof key !== 'string' || key.length === 0) {\n    throw new TypeError('pinModuleState: key must be a non-empty string');\n  }\n  const map = slots();\n  const now = Date.now();\n  const existing = map.get(key);\n  if (existing) {\n    existing.evaluations += 1;\n    existing.lastSeenAt = now;\n    return existing.value as T;\n  }\n  const value = init();\n  map.set(key, { value, evaluations: 1, firstSeenAt: now, lastSeenAt: now });\n  return value;\n}\n\n/** Read an existing pin without initializing it or counting a module evaluation. */\nexport function readPinnedModuleState<T>(key: string): T | undefined {\n  return slots().get(key)?.value as T | undefined;\n}\n\n/**\n * How many times `pinModuleState` ran for `key` in this realm.\n *\n * `0` means the module was never evaluated — which is NOT the same as \"evaluated\n * once\". A caller reporting on a module it expects to be loaded should treat `0`\n * as \"not loaded / not observable\", never as a healthy singleton.\n */\nexport function moduleEvaluationCount(key: string): number {\n  return slots().get(key)?.evaluations ?? 0;\n}\n\n/**\n * Every key whose module body was evaluated more than once — i.e. every split\n * singleton in this realm. An empty array means no duplication was observed\n * AMONG KEYS THAT USE THIS MODULE; it says nothing about modules that pin their\n * state by hand.\n *\n * Sorted by `evaluations` descending, then `key`, so the report is stable.\n */\nexport function listModuleDuplications(): ModuleDuplication[] {\n  const out: ModuleDuplication[] = [];\n  for (const [key, slot] of slots()) {\n    if (slot.evaluations > 1) {\n      out.push({\n        key,\n        evaluations: slot.evaluations,\n        firstSeenAt: slot.firstSeenAt,\n        lastSeenAt: slot.lastSeenAt,\n      });\n    }\n  }\n  out.sort((a, b) => b.evaluations - a.evaluations || a.key.localeCompare(b.key));\n  return out;\n}\n\n/** Every pinned key in this realm, duplicated or not. Diagnostics only. */\nexport function listPinnedModuleKeys(): string[] {\n  return [...slots().keys()].sort();\n}\n\n/**\n * Render a one-line human warning per duplication, or `[]` when clean.\n *\n * Kept here so every surface that reports duplication says the same thing —\n * including that a duplication is a PACKAGING fault, not a runtime error to\n * retry.\n */\nexport function formatModuleDuplicationWarnings(\n  duplications: ModuleDuplication[] = listModuleDuplications(),\n): string[] {\n  return duplications.map(\n    (d) =>\n      `SPLIT MODULE SINGLETON: '${d.key}' was evaluated ${d.evaluations}x in this process. ` +\n      `State is shared (pinned), so behavior is correct, but the duplicate module record is a ` +\n      `packaging fault — check for a bare-vs-relative import of the same file, a symlinked ` +\n      `node_modules copy, or a CJS/ESM double-load.`,\n  );\n}\n\n/**\n * Drop all pinned state in this realm. TEST-ONLY.\n *\n * Production code must never call this: it detaches live state from every module\n * record already holding a reference, which is the very split this module exists\n * to prevent.\n */\nexport function resetPinnedModuleStateForTest(): void {\n  slots().clear();\n}\n",
